def _gen_type_tick_variant(freq=1350, amp=0.16, dur=0.042):
    """
    Simulates a highly satisfying mechanical typewriter key strike (tactile mechanical click + hollow platen impact + spring ring).
    """
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    
    # 1. High-frequency tactile switch transient (metal key striking paper/platen)
    snap_n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.005)
    snap = _noise(snap_n, amp * 0.85)
    _resonant_filter(snap, 4500, 0.4, "high")
    _env_exp(snap, 1.0, 0.001, 45.0)
    _mix(buf, snap)
    
    # 2. Hollow mechanical body thud (key mechanism hitting platen roller ~280Hz)
    body = _fm(n, freq * 0.2, amp * 0.45, freq * 0.1, 1.5, decay_rate=18.0)
    _resonant_filter(body, 350, 0.5, "low")
    _env_exp(body, 1.0, 0.001, 25.0)
    _mix(buf, body)
    
    # 3. Tiny ringing steel spring ring (gives it authentic typewriter lever resonance)
    spring = _fm(n, freq * 3.5, amp * 0.28, freq * 4.5, 3.2, decay_rate=30.0)
    _env_exp(spring, 1.0, 0.001, 35.0)
    _mix(buf, spring)
    
    # Apply a tight desk-reflection slapback echo
    _apply_delay(buf, 15, feedback=0.15, wet=0.1)
    
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.2)
    return _wav(buf)

def _gen_type_tick():
    return _gen_type_tick_variant(1320, 0.75, 0.040)

def _gen_type_tick_b():
    return _gen_type_tick_variant(1560, 0.70, 0.038)

def _gen_type_tick_c():
    return _gen_type_tick_variant(1180, 0.72, 0.044)

# ── Trailer overhaul (docs/PLAN_3_AUDIO.md) - ADDITIVE ONLY ──
# New generators use existing primitives above exclusively; every legacy
# _gen_* below renders byte-identically. Registered LAZILY (startup flat).
# 100 BPM @30fps = 18 frames/beat; beat grid = 0.6 s (see TRAILER_BEAT_S).

TRAILER_BPM = 100
TRAILER_BEAT_S = 0.6

def _radio_voice(buf, kind="vasile"):
    """In-game radio treatment matching the trailer VO stem (§2.2/§2.3).

    kind: "vasile" (clean VHF van) | "volkov" (close handheld, hotter) |
    "pa" (diegetic PA horn, large hall). Mutates buf in place, returns it.
    """
    if kind == "volkov":
        _bp(buf, 350, 2200)
    elif kind == "pa":
        _bp(buf, 600, 3200)
    else:
        _bp(buf, 400, 2600)
    _mix(buf, _crackle(len(buf), 0.10, 0.50, 600, 2400), 0.3)
    _soft_clip(buf, 2.0 if kind == "volkov" else 1.5)
    if kind == "pa":
        _multitap(buf, [350, 550], [0.45, 0.35], wet=0.4)
    else:
        _multitap(buf, [60], [0.2], wet=0.2)
    return _guard_peak(buf)

def _gen_squelch_head():
    """30 ms pink burst 480-2350 Hz at -12 dB peak: radio gate opening."""
    L = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.030)
    b = _pink(L, 0.50)
    _bp(b, 480, 2350)
    _env_adsr(b, 0.10, 0.20, 0.70, 0.35, 0.60)
    return _wav(_match_peak(b, 0.25))

def _gen_squelch_tail():
    """15 ms highpassed click 3500 Hz at -18 dB peak: radio gate closing."""
    L = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.015)
    b = _pink(L, 0.50)
    _hp(b, 3500, 1)
    _env_exp(b, 1.0, 0.001, 90.0)
    return _wav(_match_peak(b, 0.126))

def _gen_riser(dur=8.0):
    """Trailer riser: sine sweep 200->2400 Hz + pink noise lowpass-swept
    300->8000 Hz in 32 chunks + accelerating ticks (8ths->32nds). Swells
    to 0.8 peak (-2 dBTP); caller hard-cuts into the 0:28.4 silence."""
    rng = random.Random(1000 + int(dur * 10))
    _ = rng  # deterministic seed reserved for future grain variation
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    tone = _sine_sweep(n, 200.0, 2400.0, 0.32)
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / float(n)
        tone[i] = int(tone[i] * (t ** 1.5))
    _mix(buf, tone)
    chunks = 32
    for c in range(chunks):
        t0 = (c * n) // chunks
        t1 = ((c + 1) * n) // chunks
        L = t1 - t0
        if L <= 0:
            continue
        cutoff = 300.0 * ((8000.0 / 300.0) ** (c / float(chunks - 1)))
        seg = _pink(L, 0.30)
        _lp(seg, cutoff, 2)
        g = ((c + 1) / float(chunks)) ** 1.5
        for i in range(L):
            seg[i] = int(seg[i] * g)
        _offset_mix(buf, seg, t0)
    n_ticks = 26
    t_start = 0.45 * dur
    for k in range(n_ticks):
        frac = k / float(n_ticks - 1)
        t = t_start + (dur * 0.53) * (frac ** 1.6)
        off = int(SAMPLE_RATE * t)
        L = min(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.012), n - off)
        if L <= 16 or off < 0:
            continue
        tick = _pink(L, 0.40)
        _bp(tick, 1800, 6500)
        _env_exp(tick, 1.0, 0.001, 120.0)
        _offset_mix(buf, tick, off, 0.5 + 0.5 * frac)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.2)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.8))

def _gen_riser_8s():
    return _gen_riser(8.0)

def _gen_riser_12s():
    return _gen_riser(12.0)

def _gen_braam(dur=1.8, f0=36.7):
    """Trailer BRAAM: D1 sine sub + octave FM pressure + 80 Hz lowpassed
    pink boom, ~1.8 s exp decay, soft-clipped, -2 dBTP peak. Hits on every
    act cut (0:07, 0:17, 0:29, 0:47)."""
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    sub = _sin(n, f0, 0.55)
    _env_exp(sub, 1.0, 0.001, 2.0)
    _mix(buf, sub)
    press = _fm(n, f0 * 2.0, 0.30, f0, 0.6, decay_rate=3.0)
    _env_exp(press, 1.0, 0.001, 2.4)
    _mix(buf, press)
    boom = _pink(n, 0.40)
    _lp(boom, 80, 3)
    _env_exp(boom, 1.0, 0.001, 2.0)
    _mix(buf, boom)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.35)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.79))

def _gen_braam_downpitch(dur=2.0):
    """End-card sting: D1->26 Hz drop + brown rumble + sparse dark taps."""
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    drop = _sine_sweep(n, 36.7, 26.0, 0.55)
    _env_exp(drop, 1.0, 0.001, 2.2)
    _mix(buf, drop)
    rum = _brown(n, 0.30)
    _lp(rum, 90, 2)
    _env_exp(rum, 1.0, 0.001, 1.8)
    _mix(buf, rum)
    _multitap(buf, [200, 420], [0.3, 0.15], wet=0.3)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.3)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.79))

def _gen_trailer_gun_suppressed():
    """M1 stealth stack (§3 SUPPRESSED_9MM): band pop + low thump +
    quiet metallic tick 5 ms early, dry (no reverb). Peaks 6 dB under the
    unsuppressed stack so the drop reads 2x louder."""
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.30)
    buf = _arr(n)
    pop = _pink(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.020), 0.9)
    _bp(pop, 500, 2600)
    _env_exp(pop, 1.0, 0.001, 60.0)
    _mix(buf, pop)
    thump = _fm(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.12), 90, 0.4, 45, 0.6, decay_rate=14.0)
    _env_exp(thump, 1.0, 0.001, 18.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, thump, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.002))
    tick = _pink(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.008), 0.35)
    _bp(tick, 2000, 7000)
    _env_exp(tick, 1.0, 0.001, 90.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, tick, 0, 0.4)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.2)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.45))

def _gen_trailer_gun_unsuppressed():
    """Post-drop stack (§3 UNSUPPRESSED): crack + FM body + snap tail."""
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.55)
    buf = _arr(n)
    crack = _pink(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.012), 1.0)
    _bp(crack, 900, 5200)
    _env_exp(crack, 1.0, 0.001, 120.0)
    _mix(buf, crack)
    body = _fm(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.30), 55, 0.7, 110, 1.6, decay_rate=7.0)
    _env_exp(body, 1.0, 0.001, 7.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, body, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.003))
    snap = _sine_sweep(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.07), 6200, 1700, 0.25)
    _env_exp(snap, 1.0, 0.001, 18.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, snap, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.010), 0.32)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.45)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.89))

def _gen_trailer_sniper_stack():
    """M2 sniper stack (§3 SNIPER): dry crack + 35 ms delayed report +
    sub bloom + 170 ms valley slap. Duck music 0.5 s after in the mix."""
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 1.15)
    buf = _arr(n)
    snap = _pink(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.006), 1.0)
    _bp(snap, 2500, 7500)
    _env_exp(snap, 1.0, 0.001, 120.0)
    _mix(buf, snap)
    blast = _brown(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.16), 0.7)
    _lp(blast, 620, 2)
    _env_exp(blast, 1.0, 0.001, 16.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, blast, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.035))
    sub = _fm(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.55), 45, 0.34, 22, 0.7, decay_rate=4.8)
    _env_exp(sub, 1.0, 0.001, 5.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, sub, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.045))
    _apply_delay(buf, 170, feedback=0.26, wet=0.18)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.4)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.89))

def _gen_trailer_breach_stack():
    """Breach stack (§3 BREACH): structural thud + pitch-dropping sub +
    inharmonic plate rattle at -5 dB. AI4 flashes on the transient."""
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.85)
    buf = _arr(n)
    thud = _brown(n, 0.65)
    _lp(thud, 170, 2)
    _env_exp(thud, 1.0, 0.001, 8.0)
    _mix(buf, thud)
    sub = _sine_sweep(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.30), 75, 34, 0.5)
    _env_exp(sub, 1.0, 0.001, 8.0)
    _mix(buf, sub)
    plate = _plate(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.30), 336.0,
                   [(1.0, 1.0), (2.71, 0.50), (5.06, 0.28)], 0.30, decay=20.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, plate, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.006), 0.56)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.4)
    return _wav(_match_peak(buf, 0.89))

TRAILER_LAZY_GENS = [
    ("squelch_head", _gen_squelch_head),
    ("squelch_tail", _gen_squelch_tail),
    ("riser_8s", _gen_riser_8s),
    ("riser_12s", _gen_riser_12s),
    ("braam", _gen_braam),
    ("braam_downpitch", _gen_braam_downpitch),
    ("trailer_gun_suppressed", _gen_trailer_gun_suppressed),
    ("trailer_gun_unsuppressed", _gen_trailer_gun_unsuppressed),
    ("trailer_sniper_stack", _gen_trailer_sniper_stack),
    ("trailer_breach_stack", _gen_trailer_breach_stack),
]
LAZY_GENS.extend(TRAILER_LAZY_GENS)

# ── Audio Manager ──

_channels = {}

# Channel 0 is reserved for voice-over (see _init_mixer / audio.voice), so
# named channels start at 1 and pygame's auto-allocation never lands a loop
# on the voice channel.
VOICE_CHANNEL_INDEX = 0


def _ch(ch_id):
    if ch_id not in _channels:
        idx = min(len(_channels) + 1, 31)
        _channels[ch_id] = pygame.mixer.Channel(idx)
    return _channels[ch_id]


# ── Upload OS CRT sounds ──

def _gen_crt_whine():
    """CRT power-on high-voltage whistle (~12 kHz flyback transformer)."""
    dur = 1.2
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    tone = _sin(n, 11800, 0.14)
    for i in range(n):
        wobble = 1.0 + 0.003 * math.sin(i * 0.0008)
        buf[i] = int(tone[i] * wobble)
    harm = _sin(n, 15750, 0.04)
    _mix(buf, harm, 0.6)
    _env_adsr(buf, 0.25, 0.15, 0.35, 0.55, 0.70)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.0)
    return _wav(buf)


def _gen_crt_thunk():
    """CRT power-off thunk: degauss coil + shadow mask settling."""
    dur = 0.35
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    thump = _fm(n, 110, 0.5, 55, 0.4, decay_rate=18.0)
    _env_exp(thump, 1.0, 0.001, 16.0)
    _mix(buf, thump)
    ring = _sin(n, 420, 0.12)
    _env_exp(ring, 1.0, 0.001, 22.0)
    _mix(buf, ring)
    click = _noise(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.008), 0.3)
    _env_exp(click, 1.0, 0.001, 60.0)
    _mix(buf, click)
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.1)
    return _wav(buf)


def _gen_modem_dialup():
    """Classic 2400 baud modem handshake (dial tone → screech → connect)."""
    rng = random.Random(7703)
    dur = 3.0
    n = int(SAMPLE_RATE * dur)
    buf = _arr(n)
    # Dial tone (0.0–0.4s).
    dt_end = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.4)
    dt = _sin(dt_end, 350, 0.12)
    dt2 = _sin(dt_end, 440, 0.10)
    for i in range(dt_end):
        dt[i] = int(dt[i] + dt2[i])
    _offset_mix(buf, dt, 0)
    # DTMF pulse (0.4–0.5s).
    dtmf_len = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.08)
    dtmf = _sin(dtmf_len, 941, 0.18)
    dtmf2 = _sin(dtmf_len, 1336, 0.15)
    for i in range(dtmf_len):
        dtmf[i] = int(dtmf[i] + dtmf2[i])
    _env_exp(dtmf, 1.0, 0.001, 30.0)
    _offset_mix(buf, dtmf, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.4))
    # Ringing (0.5–1.0s).
    ring_dur = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.5)
    rt = _sin(ring_dur, 440, 0.10)
    rt2 = _sin(ring_dur, 480, 0.09)
    for i in range(ring_dur):
        rt[i] = int(rt[i] + rt2[i])
        t = i / SAMPLE_RATE
        if not ((t < 0.15) or (0.25 < t < 0.40)):
            rt[i] = 0
    _offset_mix(buf, rt, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.5))
    # Answering carrier (1.0–1.3s).
    ced = _sin(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.3), 2100, 0.14)
    _env_adsr(ced, 0.05, 0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 0.85)
    _offset_mix(buf, ced, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 1.0))
    # Training screech (1.3–2.5s).
    sc_dur = int(SAMPLE_RATE * 1.2)
    screech = _arr(sc_dur)
    for _ in range(28):
        bl = rng.randint(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.02), int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.08))
        bo = rng.randint(0, max(1, sc_dur - bl))
        freq = rng.uniform(600, 2800)
        burst = _fm(bl, freq, 0.20, freq * rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0),
                    rng.uniform(1.0, 4.0), decay_rate=rng.uniform(8.0, 20.0))
        _env_exp(burst, 1.0, 0.001, rng.uniform(15.0, 35.0))
        _offset_mix(screech, burst, bo)
    bed = _noise(sc_dur, 0.04)
    _resonant_filter(bed, 1500, 0.3, "low")
    _mix(screech, bed)
    _soft_clip(screech, 1.2)
    _offset_mix(buf, screech, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 1.3))
    # Carrier connect (2.5–3.0s).
    carrier = _sin(int(SAMPLE_RATE * 0.5), 1650, 0.12)
    _env_adsr(carrier, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 0.5, 0.7)
    _offset_mix(buf, carrier, int(SAMPLE_RATE * 2.5))
    _soft_clip(buf, 1.1)
    return _wav(buf)


class AudioManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.sounds = {}
        self.master_volume = 0.8
        self.sfx_volume = 1.0       # 0..1 - separate scale for SFX (one-shots + loops)
        self.scheduled = []
        self._loop_channels = {}
        self._loop_base_volumes = {}
        self._duck_frames = 0
        self._duck_factor = 1.0
        self._ambience_names = {"rain", "wind", "ambient_drone",
                              "room_tone", "elec_hum", "rain_inside", "m4_roof_air"}
        self._lazy = dict(LAZY_GENS)
        self.verbose = False
        self._init_mixer()
        self._generate_all()
        
    def _ensure(self, name):
        """Build a lazily-registered sound on first use, then cache it."""
        s = self.sounds.get(name)
        if s is None and name in self._lazy:
            gen = self._lazy.pop(name)
            try:
                s = _load(gen())   # generators yield WAV bytes, like the eager path
            except Exception:
                s = None
            self.sounds[name] = s
        return s

    def _pick_footstep(self, prefix, count):
        key = f"{prefix}_{_rng_legacy.randint(1, count)}"
        return self.sounds.get(key, self.sounds.get(prefix))
        
    def _init_mixer(self):
        try:
            if not pygame.mixer.get_init():
                pygame.mixer.init(frequency=SAMPLE_RATE, size=-16, channels=2)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            pygame.mixer.set_num_channels(32)
            # Keep channel 0 out of Sound.play()'s free-channel search: it is
            # the voice-over channel. Without this a looping ambience bed
            # could grab it, and the ducking pass in update() would then
            # set_volume() the *channel* low - leaving radio VO near-silent.
            pygame.mixer.set_reserved(1)
        except Exception:
            pass
            
    def _generate_all(self):
        gens = [
            ("gunshot", _gen_gunshot),
            ("gunshot_distant", _gen_gunshot_distant),
            ("sniper_crack", _gen_sniper_crack),
            ("bullet_snap", _gen_bullet_snap),
            ("concrete_impact", _gen_concrete_impact),
            ("tinnitus", _gen_tinnitus),
            ("rifle_handle", _gen_rifle_handle),
            ("footstep", _gen_footstep),
            ("footstep_1", _gen_footstep),
            ("footstep_2", _gen_footstep_b),
            ("footstep_3", _gen_footstep_c),
            ("footstep_walk", _gen_footstep_walk),
            ("footstep_walk_1", _gen_footstep_walk),
            ("footstep_walk_2", _gen_footstep_walk_b),
            ("footstep_walk_3", _gen_footstep_walk_c),
            ("melee_hit", _gen_melee_hit),
            ("bullet_impact", _gen_bullet_impact),
            ("bullet_impact_enemy", _gen_bullet_impact_enemy),
            ("door_creak", _gen_door_creak),
            ("door_rattle", _gen_door_rattle),
            ("door_open", _gen_door_open),
            ("reload", _gen_reload),
            ("ambient_drone", _gen_ambient_drone),
            ("rain", _gen_rain),
            ("wind", _gen_wind),
            ("explosion", _gen_explosion),
            ("terminal_glitch", _gen_terminal_glitch),
            ("missile_launch", _gen_missile_launch),
            ("missile_flyby", _gen_missile_flyby),
            ("rig_impact_crack", _gen_rig_impact_crack),
            ("rig_low_boom", _gen_rig_low_boom),
            ("rig_secondary_explosion", _gen_rig_secondary_explosion),
            ("rig_metal_collapse", _gen_rig_metal_collapse),
            ("rig_water_splash", _gen_rig_water_splash),
            ("rig_fire_burst", _gen_rig_fire_burst),
            ("heartbeat", _gen_heartbeat),
            ("menu_click", _gen_menu_click),
            ("menu_hover", _gen_menu_hover),
            ("type_tick", _gen_type_tick),
            ("type_tick_1", _gen_type_tick),
            ("type_tick_2", _gen_type_tick_b),
            ("type_tick_3", _gen_type_tick_c),
            ("radio_static", _gen_radio_static),
            ("radio_chatter", _gen_radio_chatter),
            ("water_drip", _gen_water_drip),
            ("mission_complete", _gen_mission_complete),
            ("breach", _gen_breach),
            ("molotov_throw", _gen_molotov_throw),
            ("molotov_explode", _gen_molotov_explode),
            ("pickup", _gen_pickup),
            ("alarm", _gen_alarm),
            ("empty_click", _gen_empty_click),
            ("glass_shatter", _gen_glass_shatter),
            ("crt_whine", _gen_crt_whine),
            ("crt_thunk", _gen_crt_thunk),
            ("modem_dialup", _gen_modem_dialup),
        ]
        for name, gen in gens:
            try:
                self.sounds[name] = _load(gen())
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Audio gen failed: {name} - {e}")

        # Optional external Mission 3 alarm MP3.
        # Looks for:
        #   assets/alarm.mp3
        # relative to the game folder/current working directory.
        try:
            self._load_optional_sound(
                "mission3_alarm_loop",
                [
                    os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "assets", "alarm.mp3"),
                    os.path.join(os.path.abspath("."), "assets", "alarm.mp3"),
                    os.path.join(os.path.abspath("."), "First try", "assets", "alarm.mp3"),
                    os.path.join(os.path.abspath("."), "Call of Acaristan", "First try", "assets", "alarm.mp3"),
                    r"Call of Acaristan\First try\assets\alarm.mp3",
                ],
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Optional alarm.mp3 load failed: {e}")
                
    def _effective_volume(self, name, volume):
        duck = self._duck_factor if name in self._ambience_names and self._duck_frames > 0 else 1.0
        if name == "wind":
            volume *= 0.40
        elif name == "rain":
            volume *= 0.55
        elif name == "rain_inside":
            volume *= 0.50
        elif name == "room_tone":
            volume *= 0.55
        elif name == "elec_hum":
            volume *= 0.50
        # SFX scale applies to all sounds EXCEPT streaming music (which is
        # handled separately via pygame.mixer.music.set_volume). This is
        # what makes the Audio → SFX Volume slider actually audible.
        return max(0.0, min(1.0, self.master_volume * self.sfx_volume * volume * duck))

    def play(self, name, volume=1.0, loops=0, channel=None):
        if name in ("footstep", "footstep_walk", "type_tick"):
            variant = f"{name}_{_rng_legacy.randint(1, 3)}"
            s = self._ensure(variant) or self._ensure(name)
            if name == "type_tick":
                volume = min(1.0, volume * 4.5)
        else:
            s = self._ensure(name)
        if s is None:
            return None
        if self.verbose:
            print(f"[audio] {name} vol={volume:.2f}")
        vol = self._effective_volume(name, volume)
        s.set_volume(vol)
        if channel is not None:
            c = _ch(channel)
            c.play(s, loops=loops)
        else:
            c = s.play(loops=loops)
        if c and loops != 0:
            self._loop_channels[name] = c
            self._loop_base_volumes[name] = volume
        return c
        
    def play_random(self, prefix, count=3, volume=1.0, loops=0, channel=None):
        return self.play(f"{prefix}_{_rng_legacy.randint(1, count)}", volume=volume, loops=loops, channel=channel)
        
    def schedule(self, delay_frames, name, volume=1.0, loops=0, channel=None):
        self.scheduled.append({
            "delay": max(0, int(delay_frames)),
            "name": name,
            "volume": volume,
            "loops": loops,
            "channel": channel,
        })
        
    def update(self):
        for item in self.scheduled[:]:
            item["delay"] -= 1
            if item["delay"] <= 0:
                self.play(item["name"], item["volume"], item["loops"], item["channel"])
                self.scheduled.remove(item)
        if self._duck_frames > 0:
            self._duck_frames -= 1
            if self._duck_frames <= 0:
                self._duck_factor = 1.0
            for name, ch in list(self._loop_channels.items()):
                if ch is None:
                    continue
                base = self._loop0_base_volumes.get(name, 1.0) if hasattr(self, '_loop0_base_volumes') else self._loop_base_volumes.get(name, 1.0)
                try:
                    ch.set_volume(self._effective_volume(name, base))
                except Exception:
                    pass
                    
    def duck_ambience(self, frames=90, factor=0.35):
        self._duck_frames = max(self._duck_frames, int(frames))
        self._duck_factor = min(self._duck_factor, max(0.0, min(1.0, factor)))

    def duck_for_radio(self, frames=90, factor=0.35):
        """PLAN_3_AUDIO §2: duck music/ambience beds under radio VO.

        Thin wrapper over duck_ambience so radio call sites need no new
        imports; the trailer stem equivalent is the sidechaincompress
        stage in tools/render_trailer_v2.mux_1080p_trailer_mix.
        """
        self.duck_ambience(frames=frames, factor=factor)
        
    def play_3d(self, name, source_pos, listener_pos, max_dist=800, base_volume=1.0):
        s = self._ensure(name)
        if s is None:
            return None
        dx = source_pos[0] - listener_pos[0]
        dy = source_pos[1] - listener_pos[1]
        dist = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        if dist >= max_dist:
            return None
        attenuation = max(0.0, 1.0 - (dist / max_dist))
        final_vol = base_volume * self.master_volume * self.sfx_volume * attenuation
        pan = dx / max_dist
        pan = max(-1.0, min(1.0, pan))
        left_vol = final_vol * min(1.0, 1.0 - pan)
        right_vol = final_vol * min(1.0, 1.0 + pan)
        channel = s.play()
        if channel:
            channel.set_volume(left_vol, right_vol)
        return channel
        
    def stop(self, name=None, channel=None):
        # Defensive: a sound may be absent (no mixer, failed generation) and the
        # ambience layers call stop() at zone edges - this must never raise.
        if channel is not None and channel in _channels:
            try:
                _channels[channel].stop()
            except Exception:
                pass
        elif name:
            s = self.sounds.get(name)
            if s is not None:
                try:
                    s.stop()
                except Exception:
                    pass
            self._loop_channels.pop(name, None)
            self._loop_base_volumes.pop(name, None)
            
    def stop_all(self):
        for ch in _channels.values():
            ch.stop()
        for name in self.sounds:
            try:
                self.sounds[name].stop()
            except Exception:
                pass
        self._loop_channels.clear()
        self._loop_base_volumes.clear()
        self.scheduled.clear()
        self.stop_epoch = getattr(self, "stop_epoch", 0) + 1

    def hard_stop(self, music=False):
        """Silence everything NOW: one-shots, loops, scheduled cues, ducking,
        voice-over (reserved channel 0) and death screams. Called on quit,
        exit-to-menu and every mission (re)start so nothing from the old
        scene bleeds into the next one. Streaming music only if music=True."""
        self.scheduled.clear()
        self._loop_channels.clear()
        self._loop_base_volumes.clear()
        self._duck_frames = 0
        self._duck_factor = 1.0
        try:
            from audio import voice
            voice.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            pygame.mixer.unpause()       # a paused channel would resume later
            pygame.mixer.stop()          # halts reserved channels too
        except Exception:
            pass
        if music:
            self.stop_music()
        self.stop_epoch = getattr(self, "stop_epoch", 0) + 1
        
    def set_master_volume(self, vol_0_to_100):
        self.master_volume = max(0.0, min(1.0, vol_0_to_100 / 100.0))
        try:
            pygame.mixer.music.set_volume(self.master_volume * getattr(self, "_current_music_vol", 0.5))
        except Exception:
            pass
        
    def play_music(self, filename, volume=0.5):
        """Loads and streams an MP3 music track in the background."""
        import os
        filepath = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), filename)
        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
            filepath = filename
        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
            print(f"Music file not found: {filename}")
            return False
        try:
            pygame.mixer.music.load(filepath)
            self._current_music_vol = volume
            pygame.mixer.music.set_volume(self.master_volume * volume)
            pygame.mixer.music.play(loops=-1)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to play music: {e}")
            return False

    def stop_music(self):
        """Stops the streaming background music."""
        try:
            pygame.mixer.music.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def set_music_volume(self, volume):
        """Adjusts the streaming music volume dynamically."""
        self._current_music_vol = volume
        try:
            pygame.mixer.music.set_volume(self.master_volume * volume)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def set_sfx_volume(self, volume):
        """Adjusts the SFX volume scale dynamically.

        Affects all one-shot sound effects + looping ambience. Also refreshes
        any currently-looping sounds so the change is audible immediately
        rather than only on the next play().
        """
        self.sfx_volume = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(volume)))
        for name, ch in list(self._loop_channels.items()):
            if ch is None:
                continue
            base = self._loop_base_volumes.get(name, 1.0)
            try:
                ch.set_volume(self._effective_volume(name, base))
            except Exception:
                pass

    def mute_all(self):
        """Pause every playing sound + streaming music. Used by the
        Audio → Mute on Focus Loss setting when the window loses focus."""
        try:
            pygame.mixer.pause()
            pygame.mixer.music.pause()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def unmute_all(self):
        """Resume everything paused by mute_all()."""
        try:
            pygame.mixer.unpause()
            pygame.mixer.music.unpause()
        except Exception:
            pass
        
    def _load_optional_sound(self, name, candidate_paths):
        """Try to load an external sound file into self.sounds[name].

        Used for user-provided assets like assets/alarm.mp3. If loading fails,
        nothing crashes - gameplay can fall back to the procedural sound.
        """
        for path in candidate_paths:
            try:
                if path and os.path.exists(path):
                    self.sounds[name] = pygame.mixer.Sound(path)
                    print(f"Loaded optional sound '{name}': {path}")
                    return True
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Failed loading optional sound '{name}' from {path}: {e}")
        return False

    def play_mission3_alarm(self, volume=0.22):
        """Start Mission 3 lockdown alarm loop.

        The external alarm.mp3 is likely mastered loud, so this defaults LOW.
        Uses assets/alarm.mp3 if loaded as mission3_alarm_loop.
        Falls back to the procedural alarm if the MP3 is unavailable.
        """
        if "mission3_alarm_loop" in self.sounds:
            return self.play("mission3_alarm_loop", volume=volume, loops=-1, channel="m3_alarm")

        # Fallback procedural alarm, also quieter.
        return self.play("alarm", volume=min(1.0, volume * 0.65), loops=-1, channel="m3_alarm")

    def stop_mission3_alarm(self):
        """Stop Mission 3 lockdown alarm loop."""
        try:
            self.stop("mission3_alarm_loop")
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self.stop("alarm")
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            self.stop(channel="m3_alarm")
        except Exception:
            pass

    def get_sound(self, name):
        return self._ensure(name)
        
    def is_playing(self, channel):
        if channel in _channels:
            return _channels[channel].get_busy()
        return False
        
    def fadeout(self, channel, fade_ms=500):
        if channel in _channels:
            _channels[channel].fadeout(fade_ms)

    "missions.m2.draw",

    "missions.m2.world",
    "missions.m2.meta",

def __getattr__(name):
    """PEP 562 live view for rebound shared state (see _LIVE_STATE)."""
    if name in _LIVE_STATE:
        import sys as _sys2
        for _mod in _LIVE_MODULES:
            _m = _sys2.modules.get(_mod)
            if _m is not None and name in vars(_m):
                return vars(_m)[name]
    raise AttributeError(
        "module " + repr(__name__) + " has no attribute " + repr(name))

# src\core\save_system.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------


"""3-slot JSON save system for campaign progress.

Files live at the project root (not the CWD) and are written atomically via
``core.json_store`` - a crash mid-write can never corrupt the only copy.
"""
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

from core import json_store

# ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX lets two game processes run side-by-side (e.g. the
# tools/mp_arena_duo.py host + join pair) without overwriting each
# other's progress: ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX=_p1 -> save_data_p1.json.
_SAVE_SUFFIX = os.environ.get("ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX", "")
SAVE_FILE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ("save_data%s.json" % _SAVE_SUFFIX))
SLOT_COUNT = 3
_current_slot = 0

# active_mission key → (slot mission id, dossier label, flags written on completion)
_MISSION_RECORDS = {
    "MISSION1": (
        "MISSION_1",
        "Mission 1 - Black Notebook",
        {"mission1_complete": True},
    ),
    "MISSION2": (
        "MISSION_2",
        "Mission 2 - Quiet on Route 12",
        {"mission1_complete": True, "mission2_complete": True},
    ),
    "MISSION3": (
        "MISSION_3",
        "Mission 3 - The Vostral",
        {"mission1_complete": True, "mission2_complete": True,
         "mission3_complete": True},
    ),
    "MISSION4": (
        "MISSION_4",
        "Mission 4 - The Aftermath",
        {"mission1_complete": True, "mission2_complete": True,
         "mission3_complete": True, "mission4_complete": True},
    ),
    "MISSION5": (
        "MISSION_5",
        "Mission 5 - Martial Law",
        {"mission1_complete": True, "mission2_complete": True,
         "mission3_complete": True, "mission4_complete": True,
         "mission5_complete": True},
    ),
}


def _empty_slot(slot_index):
    return {
        "slot": slot_index,
        "occupied": False,
        "last_completed_mission": "",
        "last_completed_label": "No missions completed",
        "total_time": "00:00",
        "updated_at": 0,
        "progress": "",
        "stats": {},
        "flags": {},
    }


def _default_data():
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "current_slot": 0,
        "slots": [_empty_slot(i) for i in range(SLOT_COUNT)],
    }


def load_data():
    data = json_store.load_with_backup(SAVE_FILE, _default_data)
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        data = _default_data()
    slots = data.get("slots", [])
    fixed = _default_data()
    try:
        fixed["current_slot"] = max(
            0, min(SLOT_COUNT - 1, int(data.get("current_slot", 0)))
        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        pass
    for i in range(SLOT_COUNT):
        if i < len(slots) and isinstance(slots[i], dict):
            merged = _empty_slot(i)
            merged.update(slots[i])
            merged["slot"] = i
            fixed["slots"][i] = merged
    return fixed


def save_data(data):
    try:
        json_store.atomic_write(SAVE_FILE, data)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Save failed: {e}")


def select_slot(slot_index):
    global _current_slot
    idx = max(0, min(SLOT_COUNT - 1, int(slot_index)))
    _current_slot = idx
    data = load_data()
    if data.get("current_slot") != idx:
        data["current_slot"] = idx
        save_data(data)


def current_slot_index():
    return _current_slot


def get_slot(slot_index=None):
    idx = _current_slot if slot_index is None else max(0, min(SLOT_COUNT - 1, int(slot_index)))
    return load_data()["slots"][idx]


def start_new_campaign(slot_index=None):
    global _current_slot
    idx = _current_slot if slot_index is None else max(0, min(SLOT_COUNT - 1, int(slot_index)))
    _current_slot = idx
    data = load_data()
    slot = _empty_slot(idx)
    slot.update({
        "occupied": True,
        "last_completed_mission": "",
        "last_completed_label": "Campaign started - Mission 1 in progress",
        "updated_at": int(time.time()),
        "progress": "walk",
        "stats": {},
        "flags": {"mission1_started": True},
    })
    data["slots"][idx] = slot
    data["current_slot"] = idx
    save_data(data)


def set_slot_progress(progress, slot_index=None):
    """Record the coarse campaign segment ('walk' / 'm1') for resume.

    No-op when the target slot is empty so headless/dev code paths can call
    mission-start functions without creating phantom saves.
    """
    idx = _current_slot if slot_index is None else max(0, min(SLOT_COUNT - 1, int(slot_index)))
    data = load_data()
    slot = data["slots"][idx]
    if not slot.get("occupied") or slot.get("progress") == progress:
        return
    slot["progress"] = progress
    save_data(data)


def mission_complete_record(active_mission, total_time, stats=None):
    """Map an active_mission key to slot fields. Returns None if unknown."""
    rec = _MISSION_RECORDS.get(active_mission)
    if rec is None:
        print(f"save_system: unknown mission {active_mission!r} - not saving")
        return None
    mission_id, label, flags = rec
    return {
        "mission_id": mission_id,
        "label": label,
        "total_time": total_time,
        "stats": stats or {},
        "flags": dict(flags),
    }


def save_mission_complete_record(active_mission, total_time, stats=None, slot_index=None):
    """Save a mission completion from an active_mission key. False if unknown."""
    rec = mission_complete_record(active_mission, total_time, stats)
    if rec is None:
        return False
    save_mission_complete(
        rec["mission_id"],
        rec["label"],
        rec["total_time"],
        stats=rec["stats"],
        flags=rec["flags"],
        slot_index=slot_index,
    )
    return True


def save_mission_complete(mission_id, label, total_time, stats=None, flags=None, slot_index=None):
    idx = _current_slot if slot_index is None else max(0, min(SLOT_COUNT - 1, int(slot_index)))
    data = load_data()
    slot = data["slots"][idx]
    if not slot.get("occupied"):
        slot = _empty_slot(idx)
    merged_flags = dict(slot.get("flags") or {})
    merged_flags.update(flags or {})
    merged_stats = dict(slot.get("stats") or {})
    merged_stats.update(stats or {})
    slot.update({
        "occupied": True,
        "last_completed_mission": mission_id,
        "last_completed_label": label,
        "total_time": total_time,
        "updated_at": int(time.time()),
        "stats": merged_stats,
        "flags": merged_flags,
    })
    data["slots"][idx] = slot
    data["current_slot"] = idx
    save_data(data)


def format_timestamp(ts):
    if not ts:
        return "never"
    try:
        return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(ts))
    except Exception:
        return "unknown"


def has_any_save():
    return any(bool(slot.get("occupied")) for slot in load_data().get("slots", []))


# Hydrate the persisted active slot (menu panel correctness across relaunches).
try:
    _current_slot = load_data().get("current_slot", 0)
except Exception:
    _current_slot = 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src\core\settings_store.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------


"""Settings store - persistent JSON-backed user preferences.

Expanded from the original 6-field store to a full settings schema covering
Display, Audio, Gameplay, Graphics, Controls, and Accessibility. The load()
function merges saved values over a default dict, so missing keys (from old
save files) always fall back to sane defaults - no migration step needed.

save() merges the caller's dict over the currently loaded settings before
writing, so keys the caller doesn't know about (e.g. ambience_layers) are
never dropped. Writes are atomic via core.json_store.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import os

from core import json_store

# Mirrors save_system.ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX so the duo launcher can sandbox
# both files per process (settings_p1.json / settings_p2.json).
_SAVE_SUFFIX = os.environ.get("ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX", "")
SAVE_FILE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ("settings%s.json" % _SAVE_SUFFIX))

# ── Default settings ──
# Every key here MUST have a default; load() only overrides keys that exist
# in the saved JSON, so adding new keys later is always backward-compatible.
_DEFAULTS = {
    # ── Display ──
    "display_mode": 0,            # 0=Windowed, 1=Fullscreen
    "resolution_idx": 0,          # index into SETTINGS_RESOLUTIONS
    # ── Audio ──
    "master_volume": 80,
    "music_volume": 70,
    "sfx_volume": 85,
    "mute_on_focus_loss": True,
    # ── Gameplay ──
    "crosshair": True,
    "crosshair_size": 6,          # 3=small, 6=medium, 10=large
    "auto_reload": True,
    "aim_assist": False,
    "subtitles": True,
    "radio_text_size": 1,        # 0=small, 1=medium, 2=large (ui.radio)
    "radio_speaker_names": True,  # callsign plate on radio transmissions
    # ── Graphics ──
    "brightness": 50,             # 0-100, 50 = neutral
    "scanlines": True,
    "grain": True,
    "particle_density": 75,       # 0-100, scales particle counts
    # ── Controls ──
    "mouse_sensitivity": 50,      # 0-100, 50 = default
    "invert_mouse": False,
    # ── Accessibility ──
    "reduced_motion": False,
    "ambience_layers": True,   # False = no room tone/hum/drips/gusts loops
    "colorblind_mode": 0,         # 0=off, 1=protanopia, 2=deuteranopia, 3=tritanopia
    # ── Multiplayer ──
    # The name you play under in an arena match. Deliberately NOT the lobby
    # nickname: that one is what strangers see in the GLOBAL CHAT panel next
    # to a server list, this one is what goes over your head while somebody
    # is actively trying to shoot you. Empty means "not chosen yet", and the
    # arena entry panel makes you choose one.
    "player_name": "",
}


_PERCENT_KEYS = {"master_volume", "music_volume", "sfx_volume", "brightness",
                 "particle_density", "mouse_sensitivity"}
_ENUM_VALUES = {"display_mode": (0, 1), "resolution_idx": (0, 1, 2),
                "crosshair_size": (3, 6, 10), "colorblind_mode": (0, 1, 2, 3),
                "radio_text_size": (0, 1, 2)}


def _normalize(values):
    """Validate known preferences while preserving unrelated/forward-version keys."""
    result = dict(values)
    for key, default in _DEFAULTS.items():
        value = values.get(key, default)
        if type(value) is not type(default):
            value = default
        if key in _PERCENT_KEYS:
            value = max(0, min(100, value))
        elif key in _ENUM_VALUES and value not in _ENUM_VALUES[key]:
            value = default
        result[key] = value
    return result


def load():
    """Load a complete validated profile, falling back to defaults or backup."""
    saved = json_store.load_with_backup(SAVE_FILE, dict)
    return _normalize(saved if isinstance(saved, dict) else {})


def save(settings_dict):
    """Merge and write atomically. Return True only after the commit succeeds."""
    try:
        merged = load()
        merged.update(settings_dict)
        json_store.atomic_write(SAVE_FILE, _normalize(merged))
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Settings save failed: {e}")
        # An incomplete temporary file is not a saved profile.
        try:
            Path(SAVE_FILE + ".tmp").unlink(missing_ok=True)
        except OSError:
            pass
        return False


# Generous against the protocol's own cap (net/protocol.MAX_NAME_CHARS) so a
# legitimate name is never truncated by the store, but short enough that a
# hand-edited settings file cannot put a paragraph over somebody's head. The
# protocol sanitizes again on the way onto the wire; this bound is about the
# file, not the network.
PLAYER_NAME_MAX = 64


def player_name():
    """The remembered arena name, or '' when the player has not chosen one."""
    value = load().get("player_name", "")
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return ""
    return value.strip()[:PLAYER_NAME_MAX]


def set_player_name(name):
    """Remember *name* for the next session. Never raises.

    Returns what was actually stored, or '' if the write failed, so the
    caller can keep showing the typed value rather than pretending it saved.
    """
    try:
        value = str(name or "").strip()[:PLAYER_NAME_MAX]
        save({"player_name": value})
        return value
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Player name save failed: {e}")
        return ""

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src\core\user_settings.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------


"""Live user settings - shared across all gameplay modules.

acaristan.py owns the authoritative variables (loaded from settings_store) and
pushes them into this module via push_from_raw() whenever a setting changes.
Gameplay code reads SETTINGS.* so we don't have to thread 18 parameters
through every function.

Keep this module dependency-free (no pygame, no state) so it imports cleanly
from anywhere.
"""


COLORBLIND_LABELS = ("off", "protanopia", "deuteranopia", "tritanopia")


class _Settings:
    def __init__(self):
        # ── Display ──
        self.fullscreen = False
        self.brightness = 1.0          # 0.5 .. 1.5 multiplier (50 => 1.0 neutral)
        self.scanlines = True
        self.film_grain = True
        self.reduced_motion = False
        self.colorblind_mode = "off"

        # ── Audio ──
        self.master_volume = 1.0       # 0..1
        self.music_volume = 0.7
        self.sfx_volume = 0.85
        self.subtitles = True
        self.mute_on_focus_loss = True

        # ── Gameplay ──
        self.mouse_sensitivity = 1.0   # 0.25 .. 2.0
        self.invert_mouse_y = False
        self.aim_assist = False
        self.auto_reload = True
        self.particle_density = 1.0    # 0.0 .. 1.5

        # ── HUD ──
        self.show_crosshair = True
        self.crosshair_size = 6        # 3=small 6=medium 10=large (pixel half-extent)
        # NOTE: the reticle is an aiming aid and is only drawn in GAME / WALK.
        # Menu screens use the custom arrow cursor (ui.main.draw_menu_cursor)
        # instead, so there is deliberately no "crosshair in menus" option.

    def push_from_raw(self, raw: dict):
        """Update from the raw settings_store dict (0-100 ints, ints for modes).

        This is the single conversion point. acaristan.py calls this every time
        any setting changes; gameplay reads the already-converted float values.
        """
        if "display_mode" in raw:
            self.fullscreen = bool(raw["display_mode"])
        if "brightness" in raw:
            # 0..100 with 50 = neutral; map to 0.5 .. 1.5
            self.brightness = 0.5 + (raw["brightness"] / 100.0)
        if "scanlines" in raw:
            self.scanlines = bool(raw["scanlines"])
        if "grain" in raw:
            self.film_grain = bool(raw["grain"])
        if "reduced_motion" in raw:
            self.reduced_motion = bool(raw["reduced_motion"])
        if "colorblind_mode" in raw:
            idx = int(raw["colorblind_mode"])
            if 0 <= idx < len(COLORBLIND_LABELS):
                self.colorblind_mode = COLORBLIND_LABELS[idx]

        if "master_volume" in raw:
            self.master_volume = raw["master_volume"] / 100.0
        if "music_volume" in raw:
            self.music_volume = raw["music_volume"] / 100.0
        if "sfx_volume" in raw:
            self.sfx_volume = raw["sfx_volume"] / 100.0
        if "subtitles" in raw:
            self.subtitles = bool(raw["subtitles"])
        if "mute_on_focus_loss" in raw:
            self.mute_on_focus_loss = bool(raw["mute_on_focus_loss"])

        if "mouse_sensitivity" in raw:
            # 0..100 with 50 = 1.0; map to 0.25 .. 2.0 roughly linear
            self.mouse_sensitivity = max(0.25, raw["mouse_sensitivity"] / 50.0)
        if "invert_mouse" in raw:
            self.invert_mouse_y = bool(raw["invert_mouse"])
        if "aim_assist" in raw:
            self.aim_assist = bool(raw["aim_assist"])
        if "auto_reload" in raw:
            self.auto_reload = bool(raw["auto_reload"])
        if "particle_density" in raw:
            # 0..100 -> 0.0 .. 1.5 (100 = 1.5x denser than baseline)
            self.particle_density = (raw["particle_density"] / 100.0) * 1.5

        if "crosshair" in raw:
            self.show_crosshair = bool(raw["crosshair"])
        if "crosshair_size" in raw:
            self.crosshair_size = int(raw["crosshair_size"])


SETTINGS = _Settings()

def __getattr__(name):
    """PEP 562 live view for rebound shared state (see _LIVE_STATE)."""
    if name in _LIVE_STATE:
        import sys as _sys2
        for _mod in _LIVE_MODULES:
            _m = _sys2.modules.get(_mod)
            if _m is not None and name in vars(_m):
                return vars(_m)[name]
    raise AttributeError(
        "module " + repr(__name__) + " has no attribute " + repr(name))

class EmptyKeys:
    """Fake pygame.key.get_pressed() object.

    Any key lookup returns False.
    """
    def __getitem__(self, key):
        return False


def run_check(name, fn, required=True):
    try:
        fn()
        pygame.event.pump()

        if pygame.display.get_surface() is not None:
            pygame.display.flip()

    except Exception as e:
        status = "FAIL" if required else "SKIP"
        print(f"{name}: {status} {e!r}")

        if required and VERBOSE_TRACEBACKS:
            traceback.print_exc()

        return not required

    print(f"{name}: OK")
    return True


def run_import_check(module_name):
    spec = importlib.util.find_spec(module_name)

    if spec is None:
        if REQUIRE_SPLIT_MODULES:
            print(f"import {module_name}: FAIL module not found")
            return False

        print(f"import {module_name}: SKIP module not found")
        return True

    return run_check(
        f"import {module_name}",
        lambda: importlib.import_module(module_name),
        required=True,
    )


def clear_screen():
    config.screen.fill((0, 0, 0))

def check_settings_draw():
    clear_screen()
    menu.draw_menu_background()
    # Signature must mirror acaristan.py:1362-1370 exactly.
    menu.draw_settings(
        0, 0, 0,
        80, 80, 100, False,           # master, music, sfx, mute_on_focus_loss
        0, 8, True, False, True,      # crosshair, crosshair_size, auto_reload, aim_assist, subtitles
        100, True, True, 100,         # brightness, scanlines, grain, particle_density
        50, False,                    # mouse_sensitivity, invert_mouse
        False, 0,                     # reduced_motion, colorblind_mode
    )


def check_multiplayer_opens_on_server_browser():
    """Clicking MULTIPLAYER must land on the SERVER LIST, not the host panel.

    Regression guard for "MULTIPLAYER goes straight to hosting". MatchScreen
    is a single process-wide instance and every gate in app.py's
    _MultiplayerState -- handle_event, update and render -- short-circuits to
    the match screen when ``mode`` is panel/hosting/playing. Its constructor
    used to start at "panel", so the very first click on MULTIPLAYER drew the
    HOST/JOIN panel and the server browser was unreachable for the whole
    session.

    The screen's contract is: closed = browser showing, open_panel() = the
    arena panel raised on top of it.
    """
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen

    m = MatchScreen()
    assert m.mode == "closed", (
        "MatchScreen must start closed so the server browser is the landing "
        "screen, got mode=%r" % (m.mode,))
    assert not m.is_open(), "a fresh MatchScreen reports itself open"

    # A closed screen must not own input or draw anything over the browser.
    assert m.draw(config.screen) is None, "closed MatchScreen drew a frame"
    _esc = pygame.event.Event(pygame.KEYDOWN, key=pygame.K_ESCAPE,
                              unicode="\x1b")
    assert m.handle_event(_esc, (0, 0)) is False, \
        "closed MatchScreen swallowed input that belongs to the browser"

    # The arena panel raises it explicitly, and closing lowers it again so
    # the browser comes back.
    m.open_panel()
    assert m.mode == "panel" and m.is_open(), "open_panel did not raise panel"
    m.close()
    assert m.mode == "closed", "close() did not lower the panel"

    # Leaving a live match returns to the panel (map choice kept), which is
    # the documented behaviour and must not be turned into a silent close.
    m.open_panel()
    m.leave_match()
    assert m.mode == "panel", \
        "leave_match must return to the panel, got %r" % (m.mode,)
    m.close()


def check_host_is_taught_how_to_host():
    """A player who has never hosted must be told what hosting IS.

    Hosting is the one control on this screen that does not do the obvious
    thing: HOST MATCH does not put you in a game, it makes you the thing other
    people connect to, and the artefact they need (a room code) only exists
    people connect to, and the thing they need (a room code) only exists
    afterwards. The panel now spells that out, and hosting opens a frozen
    lobby with the code visible. A peer joining fills the roster but DOES NOT
    start the round; the host must press START MATCH.
    """
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen, HOST_HELP
    from ui.match_screen import PANEL_H as _H
    from ui import mp as _browser

    assert _browser.SERVER_CONNECT_Y >= (
        _browser.SERVER_SUBTITLE_Y
        + _browser.font_terminal_small.get_height() + 4), \
        "direct-connect row crowds the relay status line"
    assert (_browser.SERVER_CONNECT_Y + _browser._connect_rect.h
            <= _browser.SERVER_TAB_Y), \
        "direct-connect row overlaps the browser tabs"
    assert _browser.SERVER_LIST_TOP >= _browser.SERVER_DIVIDER_Y + 36, \
        "column headings crowd the browser divider"

    assert len(HOST_HELP) == 3, "hosting is explained in %d steps" % len(
        HOST_HELP)
    joined = " ".join(HOST_HELP).lower()
    for word in ("host", "code", "send", "join"):
        assert word in joined, "hosting steps never mention %r" % (word,)

    m = MatchScreen()
    m.open_panel()
    # The help block has to fit inside the panel, or it is drawn off the
    # bottom edge and the last step is the one nobody reads.
    assert _H >= 444, "panel too short for the hosting steps: %r" % (_H,)
    m.draw_panel(config.screen)

    # The lobby card is shared by hosts and joiners, and remains visible after
    # a peer connects until the host explicitly starts.
    m.mode = "hosting"
    m._session_phase = "lobby"
    m.room_code = "ACAR-A974P-K39GWZ"
    m.share_host = "192.168.0.5"
    m.share_port = 27015
    m._draw_waiting(config.screen)
    assert m._wait_rects.get("copy") is not None, \
        "waiting card offered no way to copy the code"

    # COPY CODE must work from the card, without opening the pause menu.
    import ui.match_screen as _ms
    _orig = _ms.clipboard_text
    m.status = ""
    try:
        _c = m._wait_rects["copy"].center
        _ev = pygame.event.Event(pygame.MOUSEBUTTONDOWN, button=1, pos=_c)
        assert m.handle_event(_ev, _c) is True, \
            "COPY CODE click was not consumed"
    finally:
        _ms.clipboard_text = _orig

    # The forwarding verdict must be one shared function: a host told the
    # code is fine on one screen and unusable on the other is worse than
    # either answer.
    m.forwarded, m.forward_note = True, ""
    ok_note, _ = m._forward_status()
    m.forwarded, m.forward_note = False, "no UPnP gateway found"
    bad_note, _ = m._forward_status()
    assert "port" in ok_note.lower() and "LAN" in bad_note, \
        "forwarding status does not distinguish public mapping from LAN-only"

    # ...and that the card's hit-rect dies with it. A rect left behind after
    # the card is gone is an invisible live button: the click where COPY CODE
    # used to be would copy instead of firing.
    m.peers.append(type("P", (), {"close": lambda self: None})())
    m._match_started = True
    m._session_phase = "playing"
    m.sim = type("S", (), {"finished": False, "scoreboard": tuple})()
    m.sess = type("Sess", (), {"local_id": 0, "world": [],
                              "sample_world": dict})()
    m.view = type("V", (), {"draw": lambda *a, **k: None})()
    m._draw_match(config.screen)
    assert m._wait_rects == {}, \
        "waiting card hit-rect survived a joining player: %r" % (
            m._wait_rects,)
    m.peers.clear()
    m.close()


def check_remote_input_is_applied():
    """A REMOTE player's input must reach the simulation.

    This is the check that catches the worst multiplayer bug there is: the
    host accepting packets, acknowledging them, and quietly throwing them
    away. Both the host's own keyboard input and the host-side read path
    build packets containing the "t" field, so anything that re-parses
    after a parse strips it and the validation then rejects the packet --
    leaving local play working perfectly while no remote player can move or
    shoot. It looks exactly like "the netcode is fine, the sim is fine".
    """
    import socket as _socket
    from net import protocol as _P
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen as _MS

    m = _MS()
    m.open_panel()
    m.players = 4
    m.request_host(0)
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    idle = (500, 350, False)
    m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
    port = m.srv.getsockname()[1]
    conn = None
    try:
        conn = _socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=5)
        conn.setblocking(False)
        # A connection is only a CANDIDATE until it sends the join handshake;
        # without it the host must not create a player (see the phantom-peer
        # regression check).
        conn.sendall(_P.encode(_P.make_join_match()))
        for _ in range(8):          # let the host accept
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert len(m.peers) == 1, "remote player never joined"
        assert sorted(m.sim.players) == [0, 1], \
            "sim roster wrong: %r" % sorted(m.sim.players)

        from missions import arena as _AR
        st = m.sim.players[1]
        _AR._grant(st, _P.WPN_OS12)
        st["weapon"] = _P.WPN_PISTOL
        x0 = st["x"]
        y0 = st["y"]

        # Even hostile/stale input packets during the lobby are ignored.
        for f in range(20):
            conn.sendall(_P.encode(_P.make_input(f, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0)))
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert st["x"] == x0 and st["y"] == y0, \
            "remote input moved a player while the host was in the lobby"
        assert m.sim.tick == 0, "the lobby advanced the authoritative clock"

        assert m._begin_countdown(), "host could not start after a peer joined"
        ammo_before_intro = st["ammo"]
        for f in range(20, 240):
            # Movement, fire, reload and a valid weapon switch must not be
            # buffered for the first live tick.
            conn.sendall(_P.encode(_P.make_input(
                f, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, _P.F_FIRING | _P.F_RELOAD,
                cycle=True)))
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if m.session_phase() == "playing":
                break
            assert st["x"] == x0 and st["y"] == y0, \
                "remote player moved during the host countdown"
            assert st["ammo"] == ammo_before_intro, \
                "remote player fired during the host countdown"
        assert m.session_phase() == "playing", \
            "host countdown did not release the simulation"
        assert st["x"] == x0 and st["y"] == y0, \
            "countdown movement leaked onto the first live tick"
        assert st["ammo"] == ammo_before_intro, \
            "countdown firing leaked onto the first live tick"
        assert st["weapon"] == _P.WPN_PISTOL, \
            "countdown weapon switch leaked onto the first live tick"

        # MOVE: hold east for a second of live ticks.
        for f in range(60):
            conn.sendall(_P.encode(
                _P.make_input(100 + f, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0)))
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert st["x"] > x0 + 4, \
            "remote input ignored after Start: x stayed %.1f (was %.1f)" % (st["x"], x0)

        # FIRE: hold the trigger and check the magazine is spent.
        ammo0 = st["ammo"]
        shots = 0
        for f in range(120):
            conn.sendall(_P.encode(_P.make_input(
                1000 + f, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0,
                _P.F_FIRING if f < 100 else 0)))
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if m.sim.last_shot is not None:
                shots += 1
                # last_shot is per-tick and must carry the shooter id.
                assert len(m.sim.last_shot) == 6, \
                    "last_shot shape changed: %r" % (m.sim.last_shot,)
                assert m.sim.last_shot[4] == 1, \
                    "last_shot shooter id wrong: %r" % (m.sim.last_shot[4],)
        assert shots > 0, "remote player never fired"
        assert st["ammo"] < ammo0, "remote trigger did not spend ammo"
    finally:
        if conn is not None:
            try:
                conn.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
        m.close()


def check_lobby_relay_is_not_a_player():
    """The lobby relay's own connection must never become an opponent.

    The game keeps a relay client running while a match is hosted, and that
    client retries a FIXED local master address forever. When the match
    listener shared the relay's port, its reconnect was accepted as a
    player: a "bot" that never moved appeared, and the frozen waiting lobby
    ended even though nobody had joined. An accepted socket is now only a
    candidate until it sends the join handshake.
    """
    import socket as _socket
    from net import protocol as _P
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen

    m = MatchScreen()
    m.open_panel()
    m.players = 4
    m.request_host(0)
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    idle = (500, 350, False)
    m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
    port = m.srv.getsockname()[1]
    conn = None
    try:
        conn = _socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=5)
        conn.setblocking(False)
        for _ in range(8):
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        # Accepted, but not a player: no roster entry, no round.
        assert not m.peers, "an unannounced connection became a player"
        assert sorted(m.sim.players) == [0], "phantom player in the sim roster"
        assert m.waiting_for_player(), "the waiting lobby ended for a stranger"
        assert m.sim.tick == 0, "the round started with nobody in it"

        # The relay speaks the LOBBY protocol (hello + query), not the match
        # protocol. Sending it must close the connection, not seat it.
        conn.sendall(_P.encode({"t": _P.T_HELLO, "user": "operator",
                                "proto": _P.PROTO_VERSION}))
        conn.sendall(_P.encode({"t": _P.T_QUERY}))
        for _ in range(8):
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert not m.peers, "a lobby client was seated as a player"
        assert sorted(m.sim.players) == [0], "lobby client entered the sim"
        assert m.waiting_for_player(), "the waiting lobby ended for the relay"
        assert m.sim.tick == 0, "a lobby client started the round"
        # It must be CLOSED, not merely ignored, so the slot is free again
        # and the relay's retry cycle cannot pile up sockets.
        conn.settimeout(2.0)
        try:
            data = conn.recv(65536)
        except OSError:
            data = b""      # RST is also a closed connection
        assert data == b"", "the stray connection was left open"

        # A genuine client on the same listener still gets in, so the guard
        # did not simply break joining.
        good = _socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=5)
        good.sendall(_P.encode(_P.make_join_match()))
        for _ in range(8):
            m.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert len(m.peers) == 1, "a real match client was rejected"
        assert m.peers[0].player_id == 1, "real client got the wrong slot"
        assert m.waiting_for_player(), \
            "joining automatically started the round instead of opening a lobby"
        assert m.sim.tick == 0, "a joined player advanced the frozen lobby"
        assert len(m._lobby_roster()) == 2, \
            "the lobby roster did not include host and joining player"
        good.close()
    finally:
        if conn is not None:
            try:
                conn.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
        m.close()


def check_client_join_completes():
    """Clients join a lobby; only the host can start the frozen countdown.

    This drives a real MatchScreen client against a real host over loopback:
    socket assignment, initial static snapshot, room roster, explicit host
    start, synchronized 3/2/1/GO, and then the first live simulation tick.
    """
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen
    from net import roomcode as _RC

    host = MatchScreen()
    host.open_panel()
    host.players = 2
    # Real names, so the roster assertion below also proves the name crossed
    # the wire. With slot labels it only proved two slots existed.
    host.player_name = "HOSTNAME"
    host.request_host(0)               # ephemeral; no router touch
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    idle = (500, 350, False)
    host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
    assert host.mode == "hosting", "host did not start: " + host.status
    assert host.waiting_for_player(), "host should start in the waiting lobby"
    host.update(keys, (500, 350, True), 0.1)
    assert host.sim.tick == 0, "host simulation advanced before anyone joined"
    port = host.srv.getsockname()[1]

    client = MatchScreen()
    client.open_panel()
    client.player_name = "JOINER"
    client.request_join(_RC.encode("127.0.0.1", port))
    try:
        for _ in range(180):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if client.sess is not None and client.sess.local_id == 1 \
                    and client.mode == "playing" \
                    and client.sess.sample_world():
                break
        assert client.mode == "playing", (
            "client never entered the room (mode=%r status=%r)"
            % (client.mode, client.status))
        # Connection alone only creates the lobby: both sides must remain
        # frozen and the client must receive the two-player roster.
        assert host.waiting_for_player(), \
            "a client joining auto-started the match"
        assert host.sim.tick == 0, "simulation advanced before host Start"
        assert client.in_match_lobby(), \
            "joiner did not remain on the shared pre-game lobby"
        assert client._match_state.get("roster") == [
            (0, "HOSTNAME"), (1, "JOINER")], \
            "joiner did not receive the host's player roster: %r" % (
                client._match_state.get("roster"),)
        assert client.sess.local_id == 1, \
            "client never learned its slot: %r" % client.sess.local_id
        assert len(host.peers) == 1, "host never accepted the client"
        assert client.sess.sample_world(), "client received no lobby world"

        host._draw_waiting(config.screen)
        start_rect = host._lobby_rects.get("start")
        assert start_rect is not None, \
            "host lobby did not show START MATCH with two players"
        click = pygame.event.Event(pygame.MOUSEBUTTONDOWN, button=1,
                                   pos=start_rect.center)
        assert host.handle_event(click, start_rect.center), \
            "START MATCH click was not consumed"
        assert host.session_phase() == "countdown", \
            "host click did not start the countdown"
        frozen_pos = tuple(host.sim.players[1][k] for k in ("x", "y"))
        frozen_ammo = host.sim.players[1]["ammo"]

        class _HeldKeys(dict):
            def __missing__(self, key):
                return key in (pygame.K_w, pygame.K_d)

        held = _HeldKeys()
        for _ in range(260):
            host.update(keys, (500, 350, True), 1.0 / 60.0)
            client.update(held, (500, 350, True), 1.0 / 60.0)
            if host.session_phase() == "playing" and \
                    client.session_phase() == "playing":
                break
            assert host.sim.tick == 0, \
                "host simulation ticked before the countdown finished"
            assert tuple(host.sim.players[1][k] for k in ("x", "y")) == frozen_pos, \
                "remote player moved during the lobby/countdown"
            assert host.sim.players[1]["ammo"] == frozen_ammo, \
                "remote player fired during the lobby/countdown"
        assert host.session_phase() == "playing", \
            "host did not enter gameplay after the countdown"
        assert client.session_phase() == "playing", \
            "client did not receive the host's live phase"
        for _ in range(3):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert host.sim.tick > 0, "simulation did not resume after GO"
        assert client.sess.sample_world(), "client lost the world after GO"
    finally:
        client.close()
        host.close()


def check_host_left_ends_session():
    """A host that leaves must end the session for every client in it.

    The host IS the simulation and there is no host migration, so its
    departure is not "a player left", it is "the match no longer exists".
    Two ways of getting that wrong are covered here.

    Silence: a host that loses power never sends FIN or RST, so a client
    that only reacts to the socket dying waits in a frozen arena forever.

    Ambiguity: even a clean socket close tells the client nothing about
    WHY -- its own wifi dropping looks identical -- so the host now says
    the session is over before it closes, and the client leaves with an
    explanation instead of a guess.
    """
    import time as _time
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen, HOST_SILENCE_TIMEOUT
    from net import roomcode as _RC
    from net import protocol as _P

    assert _P.parse_host_left(_P.make_host_left("gone")) == "gone", \
        "host-left packet did not carry its reason"
    assert _P.parse_host_left({"t": _P.T_HOST_LEFT}) == "", \
        "a reasonless host-left packet is still a complete answer"
    assert _P.parse_host_left({"t": "snap"}) is None, \
        "a snapshot was mistaken for a host-left packet"

    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    idle = (500, 350, False)

    host = MatchScreen()
    host.open_panel()
    host.players = 2
    host.request_host(0)
    host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
    port = host.srv.getsockname()[1]

    client = MatchScreen()

    def _rejoin():
        """Join (or re-join) the host and wait until the slot is assigned."""
        client.open_panel()
        client.request_join(_RC.encode("127.0.0.1", port))
        for _ in range(180):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if client.mode == "playing" and client.sess.local_id == 1:
                return
        raise AssertionError("client never joined: " + client.status)

    try:
        _rejoin()
        # (1) A host that goes quiet. No packet, no RST, just nothing.
        assert client._last_recv is not None, \
            "client never armed its host-silence watchdog"
        client._last_recv = _time.monotonic() - (HOST_SILENCE_TIMEOUT + 1.0)
        client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert client.mode != "playing", \
            "a silent host left the client sitting in a dead match"
        assert "host" in client.status.lower(), \
            "the client was not told why it left: %r" % (client.status,)

        # (2) A host that leaves cleanly. The announcement has to reach the
        # client before the sockets it rides on are closed.
        _rejoin()
        host.close()
        for _ in range(60):
            client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if client.mode != "playing":
                break
        assert client.mode != "playing", \
            "the client was still in the match after the host left"
        assert "host" in client.status.lower(), \
            "the client was not told the host ended it: %r" % (client.status,)
        assert client.sock is None and client.sess is None, \
            "leaving an ended session leaked its socket"
    finally:
        client.close()
        host.close()


def check_switch_survives_batched_inputs():
    """Switches must survive network batching and apply only once.

    Gameplay input is sampled every rendered frame, but TCP may deliver two
    frames in one read. A switch is a one-shot action: taking only the latest
    input erases it if a neutral frame follows; reusing the same latest input
    for catch-up simulation ticks cycles twice and lands back on the start.
    """
    from net.match import MatchSession
    from net import protocol as P
    from missions import arena as AR

    class _Sink:
        def _send(self, obj):
            return True

    sess = MatchSession(_Sink(), is_host=True)
    sim = AR.ArenaSim(sess, AR.ARENA_YARD, score_limit=99)
    st = sim.add_player(1, "CLIENT")
    AR._grant(st, P.WPN_OS12)
    st["weapon"] = P.WPN_PISTOL

    # Two inputs land in the same host read before it runs the next tick.
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(1, 0, 0, 0, cycle=True), peer_id=1)
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(2, 0, 0, 0), peer_id=1)
    sim.step()
    assert st["weapon"] == P.WPN_OS12, \
        "a neutral frame batched behind Q erased the switch"
    sim.step()
    assert st["weapon"] == P.WPN_OS12, \
        "a catch-up tick applied the same switch a second time"

    # Even if the host has no new packet for several ticks, Q is a single
    # tap, not a held direction; it must not ping-pong between guns.
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(3, 0, 0, 0, cycle=True), peer_id=1)
    for _ in range(4):
        sim.step()
    assert st["weapon"] == P.WPN_PISTOL, \
        "a single Q tap was reapplied across host simulation ticks"

    # Direct number-key requests can be batched as well; don't lose one just
    # because another input arrived before the next host update.
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(4, 0, 0, 0, weapon=P.WPN_OS12), peer_id=1)
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(5, 0, 0, 0), peer_id=1)
    sim.step()
    assert st["weapon"] == P.WPN_OS12, \
        "a neutral frame batched behind a number key erased the switch"

    # Player IDs are recycled. A departed player's queued Q must not equip
    # a weapon for the next connection that inherits that slot.
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(6, 0, 0, 0, cycle=True), peer_id=1)
    sess.forget_peer(1)
    sess._accept_input(P.make_input(0, 0, 0, 0), peer_id=1)
    assert not sess.consume_input(1).get("wcycle"), \
        "a departed player's queued switch reached the replacement peer"

    # Through the *real* host socket read path, too. A direct _accept_input
    # test alone would miss a regression where the host drops an earlier
    # packet while parsing several newline frames from a single TCP recv.
    import socket
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen

    host = MatchScreen()
    host.open_panel()
    host.players = 2
    host.request_host(0)
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    idle = (500, 350, False)
    host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
    conn = None
    try:
        conn = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1",
                                         host.srv.getsockname()[1]), timeout=3)
        conn.sendall(P.encode(P.make_join_match()))
        for _ in range(8):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert len(host.peers) == 1, "host did not accept the real client"
        assert host.waiting_for_player(), \
            "a raw client connection started the match without host input"
        assert host._begin_countdown(), "host could not start with a joined player"
        for _ in range(240):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if host.session_phase() == "playing":
                break
        assert host.session_phase() == "playing", \
            "host never reached live play after explicit start"
        player = host.sim.players[1]
        AR._grant(player, P.WPN_OS12)
        player["weapon"] = P.WPN_PISTOL
        # Deliver the tap and its next neutral frame in a single TCP write.
        conn.sendall(P.encode(P.make_input(1, 0, 0, 0, cycle=True))
                     + P.encode(P.make_input(2, 0, 0, 0)))
        for _ in range(8):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert player["weapon"] == P.WPN_OS12, \
            "batched switch disappeared on the real host socket"
    finally:
        if conn is not None:
            conn.close()
        host.close()


def check_weapon_switching_in_match():
    """A player must be able to switch weapons mid-match.

    Switching is a request, never an order: the host owns the loadout, so
    a client that names a gun it never picked up is refused -- otherwise
    every weapon crate on the map is pointless, because the gun is free.
    What the request does need is to actually ARRIVE. The cycle request
    (Q / wheel) was dropped in validation and never reached the host at
    all, so the key did nothing and there was no way to tell why.
    """
    from ui.match_screen import MatchScreen
    from net import roomcode as _RC
    from net import protocol as _P
    from missions import arena as _AR

    # The cycle flag has to survive the wire, or the host never sees it.
    assert _P.parse_input(_P.make_input(1, 0, 0, 0.0, cycle=True)).get(
        "wcycle") == 1, "cycle request was stripped in validation"
    assert "c" not in _P.make_input(1, 0, 0, 0.0), \
        "an idle packet grew a cycle field"

    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    idle = (500, 350, False)
    host = MatchScreen()
    host.open_panel()
    host.players = 2
    host.request_host(0)
    host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
    port = host.srv.getsockname()[1]

    client = MatchScreen()
    client.open_panel()
    client.request_join(_RC.encode("127.0.0.1", port))
    try:
        for _ in range(180):
            host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
            if client.mode == "playing" and client.sess.local_id == 1:
                break
        assert client.mode == "playing", "client never joined: " + client.status
        assert client.in_match_lobby(), \
            "joining should show the pre-game lobby, not live gameplay"

        def pump(n=90):
            for _ in range(n):
                host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
                client.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)

        # Gameplay controls are swallowed in the lobby and countdown. They
        # must not turn into pending requests after the host presses Start.
        q = pygame.event.Event(pygame.KEYDOWN, key=pygame.K_q)
        client.handle_event(q, (500, 350))
        assert not client._want_cycle and not client._toast, \
            "lobby input leaked through to weapon handling"
        assert host._begin_countdown(), "host could not start after the join"
        pump(2)
        assert client.session_phase() == "countdown", \
            "joiner did not receive the host-owned countdown"
        client.handle_event(q, (500, 350))
        assert not client._want_cycle, \
            "countdown input queued a weapon switch"
        for _ in range(240):
            pump()
            if (host.session_phase() == "playing"
                    and client.session_phase() == "playing"):
                break
        assert host.session_phase() == client.session_phase() == "playing", \
            "host and client did not leave the frozen countdown together"
        client.handle_event(q, (500, 350))
        assert "PICK UP" in client._toast, \
            "Q with only the spawn pistol gave no explanation in live play"

        # Collect actual weapon crates, not a synthetic _grant call: a
        # freshly spawned player only owns the pistol and Q cannot switch
        # until they collect another gun. Exercise the real pickup path.
        st = host.sim.players[1]
        rifle = next(pk for pk in host.sim.pickup_items
                     if pk["kind"] == "weapon"
                     and pk["value"] == _P.WPN_OS12)
        st["x"], st["y"] = rifle["x"], rifle["y"]
        host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert _P.WPN_OS12 in _AR.owned_weapons(st), \
            "the client did not collect the OS-12 crate"
        st["weapon"] = _P.WPN_PISTOL
        host_st = host.sim.players[0]
        smg = next(pk for pk in host.sim.pickup_items
                   if pk["kind"] == "weapon" and pk["value"] == _P.WPN_K9)
        host_st["x"], host_st["y"] = smg["x"], smg["y"]
        host.update(keys, idle, 1.0 / 60.0)
        assert _P.WPN_K9 in _AR.owned_weapons(host_st), \
            "the host did not collect the K-9 crate"
        host_st["weapon"] = _P.WPN_PISTOL

        # The loadout has to reach the client, or it cannot grey out the
        # keys the host is going to refuse.
        pump(60)
        assert _P.WPN_OS12 in client._local_carry(), \
            "client never learned what it is carrying: %r" % (
                client._local_carry(),)

        # 2 = the OS-12 we just picked up.
        client.handle_event(pygame.event.Event(pygame.KEYDOWN,
                                              key=pygame.K_2), (500, 350))
        assert client._want_weapon == _P.WPN_OS12, "number key did not arm"
