# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_arena_duo.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Launch TWO full game windows already sitting in the multiplayer arena.

    tools/mp_arena_duo.py            # yard, 1v1, ports 27017
    tools/mp_arena_duo.py --map crossfire --players 4

Player 1 hosts, player 2 joins 127.0.0.1:<port>. Both windows boot with
--dev-mp-host / --dev-mp-join so the arena panel is already raised and
connected - no menu clicks. Press START MATCH on the host window to play.

Save files are sandboxed per window (ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX=_p1/_p2) so the two
processes never overwrite each other's save_data.json / settings.json
(see docs/KRAPNET_MULTIPLAYER.md - launching the game twice used to be
the documented way to corrupt your save).

Why two real windows instead of the headless bot: tools/mp_bot.py only
speaks lobby chat - it cannot move/shoot in an arena. Running the real
renderer + real ArenaSim over a real socket on loopback is the only way
to feel input latency, camera, fire rate and prediction with 2 players.
"""
import argparse
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ACARISTAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "acaristan.py")


def _launch(env_extra, *game_args):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(env_extra)
    # Side-by-side windows so both arenas are visible at once.
    cmd = [sys.executable, ACARISTAN] + list(game_args)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=ROOT, env=env)
    # Stagger the boots so the host's listener exists before P2 dials in.
    time.sleep(1.0)
    return proc


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Boot 2 games into one arena")
    ap.add_argument("--map", default="yard",
                    help="arena map both windows use (default: yard)")
    ap.add_argument("--players", type=int, default=2,
                    help="seat cap, host included (2-8, default: 2)")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=27017,
                    help="match port P1 hosts on (default: 27017)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.players = max(2, min(8, args.players))

    procs = []
    try:
        print("[duo] P1 hosting %s on 127.0.0.1:%d ..." % (args.map, args.port))
        procs.append(_launch(
            {"ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX": "_p1"},
            "--dev-mp-host",
            "--mp-map", args.map,
            "--mp-players", str(args.players),
            "--mp-port", str(args.port),
        ))
        print("[duo] P2 joining 127.0.0.1:%d ..." % args.port)
        procs.append(_launch(
            {"ACA_SAVE_SUFFIX": "_p2"},
            "--dev-mp-join", "127.0.0.1:%d" % args.port,
            "--mp-map", args.map,
            "--mp-players", str(args.players),
        ))
        print("[duo] Both windows up. START MATCH on the P1 (host) window.")
        print("[duo] Ctrl+C here kills both windows.")
        while True:
            time.sleep(1.0)
            if any(p.poll() is not None for p in procs):
                print("[duo] A window closed - shutting down the other.")
                break
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n[duo] Stopping both windows ...")
    finally:
        for p in procs:
            try:
                if p.poll() is None:
                    p.terminate()
            except OSError:
                pass
        for p in procs:
            try:
                p.wait(timeout=5)
            except Exception:
                try:
                    p.kill()
                except OSError:
                    pass
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_bot.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Headless fake player, for testing multiplayer on ONE PC.

Launching the game twice on one machine is a bad way to test this: both
instances share save_data.json and settings.json, so the second one
overwrites the first's progress and settings on exit. This tool avoids
that entirely -- it speaks the real protocol over a real socket, so it
exercises exactly the code path a second player would, without pygame,
a window, or touching your save file.

Typical use -- start tools/mp_host.py, open the game on Multiplayer, then:

    python tools/mp_bot.py                       # join and sit there
    python tools/mp_bot.py --say hi there        # join and say something
    python tools/mp_bot.py --name Biribel --every 8 --count 5

Every line the bot sends is echoed by the master and should appear in the
game's chat panel, which is the point: it proves the whole loop
(bot -> socket -> host -> your game) without a second human.
"""

import argparse
import os
import random
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "src"))

from net import protocol as P  # noqa: E402
from net.client import MPRelayClient  # noqa: E402

CHATTER = [
    "anyone else here?",
    "lobby works",
    "gg",
    "testing 1 2 3",
    "can you see this",
    "hello from the other pc (same pc)",
    "we're connected!",
    "no gameplay yet, but chat is real",
]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fake player for MP testing")
    ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=P.DEFAULT_MASTER_PORT)
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="Tester2")
    ap.add_argument("--say", action="append", default=[],
                    help="send this line (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--every", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="auto-send chatter every N seconds")
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=0,
                    help="stop after this many auto lines (0 = forever)")
    ap.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="exit after N seconds (0 = until Ctrl+C)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    received = []
    client = MPRelayClient(host=args.host, port=args.port,
                           nickname=args.name, chat_enabled=True)

    # Reuse the same hook the game uses, so this sees identical messages.
    import net.client as _C
    _C.register_chat_sink(lambda m: received.append(m))

    print("Connecting to %s:%d as %r ..." % (args.host, args.port, args.name))
    client.start()
    client.request_connect()

    deadline = time.time() + 10
    while time.time() < deadline:
        status, error, servers, _nick = client.state()
        if status == "online":
            break
        if status == "error" and error:
            print("  could not connect: %s" % error)
            print("  is the host running?  python tools\\mp_host.py")
            client.stop()
            return 1
        time.sleep(0.2)
    else:
        print("  timed out")
        client.stop()
        return 1

    status, error, servers, nick = client.state()
    print("Connected. Host reports %d server(s):" % len(servers))
    for name, cur, mx, ping, _rules in servers:
        print("    %-40s %d/%d  %dms" % (name[:40], cur, mx, ping))
    print("Now switch to the game (Multiplayer). Ctrl+C here to leave.\n")

    for line in args.say:
        client.send_chat(line)
        print("  sent: %s" % line)
        time.sleep(0.3)

    sent = 0
    end_at = time.time() + args.seconds if args.seconds else None
    try:
        while True:
            # Echo anything the game's chat panel sent us, so you can see
            # traffic flowing in both directions from one terminal.
            while received:
                msg = received.pop(0)
                if msg.get("user") != args.name:
                    print("  <%s> %s" % (msg.get("user"), msg.get("text")))
            if args.every and (not args.count or sent < args.count):
                now = time.time()
                if now >= (getattr(main, "_next", 0.0)):
                    line = random.choice(CHATTER)
                    if client.send_chat(line):
                        print("  sent: %s" % line)
                        sent += 1
                    main._next = now + args.every
            if end_at and time.time() >= end_at:
                break
            if args.count and sent >= args.count and not args.every:
                # Nothing left to do and no linger requested.
                if not received:
                    break
            time.sleep(0.2)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        print("\nLeaving.")
        client.stop()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_choreo_probe.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""mp_choreo_probe.py - gate the MP trailer fight headlessly before capturing.

Runs the REAL ScriptDriver from mp_trailer_capture against the REAL ArenaSim
on foundry with no renderer, no sockets and no ffmpeg, and reports the things
the trailer actually depends on. Turns a ~50 s capture into a 2 s loop.

Gates, per seed:
  * first shot inside 2 s of GO          (was 7.5 s)
  * no silent gap over 2.5 s             (was 4.8 s)
  * every seat pulls the trigger, 5+ shots - a fair-looking scoreboard will
    happily hide a seat that never fires, which is exactly what went wrong
  * both teams score
  * neither team goes more than 5.5 s without a kill, or the killfeed stalls

Usage:  python tools/mp_choreo_probe.py
"""
import math
import os
import random
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
os.chdir(ROOT)
os.environ.setdefault("SDL_VIDEODRIVER", "dummy")
os.environ.setdefault("SDL_AUDIODRIVER", "dummy")
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))

import mp_trailer_capture as C                     # noqa: E402
from missions import arena as AR                    # noqa: E402
from net import protocol as P                       # noqa: E402

T = C.SIM_HZ
SEEDS = (20261004, 7, 4242, 99, 31337)
GATE_FIRST_SHOT = 2.0
GATE_MAX_GAP = 2.5
GATE_MIN_SHOTS = 5
GATE_MAX_SCORELULL = 5.5


class StubSession:
    """The handful of ArenaSim.session hooks a local dry-run needs."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.tick = 0
        self.world = None
        self.is_host = True
        self.local_id = 0
        self.inputs = {}

    def consume_input(self, pid):
        return self.inputs.get(pid)

    def send_events(self, tick, events):
        pass

    def broadcast(self):
        pass


def run(seconds=16.0, seed=20261004, verbose=False):
    nav = C.GridNav(AR.ARENAS[C.MAP_NAME])
    sess = StubSession()
    sim = AR.ArenaSim(sess, AR.ARENAS[C.MAP_NAME], map_name=C.MAP_NAME,
                      mode=C.MODE_NAME)

    order = [(0, C.HOST_NAME), (1, "BIRIBEL"), (2, C.FRIEND_NAME),
             (3, "MICUL FUEGO")]
    for pid, nick in order:
        sim.add_player(pid, nick)
    nick_of = {pid: p["nick"] for pid, p in sim.players.items()}

    # The same opening stance phase_combat applies on the real capture.
    for pid, nick in nick_of.items():
        key = C.seat_key(nick)
        post = C.FOUNDRY_POSTS.get(key) if key else None
        if post is None:
            continue
        px, py = C._tc(*post)
        p = sim.players[pid]
        p["x"], p["y"] = float(px), float(py)
        p["dead"] = False
        p["hp"] = AR.MAX_HP
        sim.rules.spawned_at[pid] = sim.tick - AR.SPAWN_PROTECT_TICKS

    scripts = C.foundry_scripts()
    drivers = {}
    for pid, nick in nick_of.items():
        key = C.seat_key(nick)
        spec, restart = scripts[key]
        post = C.FOUNDRY_POSTS.get(key)
        drivers[pid] = C.ScriptDriver(pid, nav, lambda: sim, spec,
                                      random.Random(seed + pid),
                                      restart_at=restart,
                                      home=C._tc(*post) if post else None)

    total = int(seconds * T)
    shots, kills, seen = [], [], set()
    motion = {pid: dict(distance=0.0, minx=sim.players[pid]["x"],
                        maxx=sim.players[pid]["x"], miny=sim.players[pid]["y"],
                        maxy=sim.players[pid]["y"]) for pid in sim.players}
    previous = {}
    consumed = 0
    hist = [0] * int(seconds)
    last_sec = [-1]

    for i in range(total):
        sess.inputs = {}
        for pid, d in drivers.items():
            (ax, ay), aim, fire, want, sprint = d.think()
            st = sim.players[pid]
            if st.get("dead"):
                continue
            aim_deg = math.degrees(math.atan2(aim[1] - st["y"],
                                               aim[0] - st["x"])) % 360.0
            # ArenaSim consumes the wire-format angle field ``a`` (the same
            # conversion HeadlessBot uses). Raw aim coordinates are not a
            # recognized simulation input and silently left shots at 0 deg.
            sess.inputs[pid] = dict(mx=ax, my=ay, a=aim_deg,
                                    b=(P.F_FIRING if fire else 0)
                                    | (P.F_SPRINTING if sprint else 0),
                                    w=want)
        sim.step()
        for pid, st in sim.players.items():
            if st.get("dead"):
                previous.pop(pid, None)
                continue
            d = drivers[pid]
            if d._was_dead:  # ignore the single respawn frame before restaging
                previous.pop(pid, None)
                continue
            x, y = st["x"], st["y"]
            old = previous.get(pid)
            if old is not None and math.hypot(x - old[0], y - old[1]) > 20.0:
                # A respawn restage is a teleport, not authored footwork.
                previous[pid] = (x, y)
                continue
            box = motion[pid]
            box["minx"] = min(box["minx"], x)
            box["maxx"] = max(box["maxx"], x)
            box["miny"] = min(box["miny"], y)
            box["maxy"] = max(box["maxy"], y)
            if old is not None:
                box["distance"] += math.hypot(x - old[0], y - old[1])
            previous[pid] = (x, y)

        n = len(sim.shots)
        for shot in sim.shots[consumed:]:
            shots.append((sim.tick, shot[4]))
            hist[min(len(hist) - 1, sim.tick // T)] += 1
        consumed = n
        for ev in sim.events:
            if ev[0] == P.EV_KILL:
                key = (ev[1], ev[2], sim.tick)
                if key not in seen:
                    seen.add(key)
                    kills.append((sim.tick, ev[1], ev[2]))

        sec = min(len(hist) - 1, sim.tick // T)
        if verbose and sec != last_sec[0]:
            last_sec[0] = sec
            rows = []
            for pid in sorted(sim.players):
                st = sim.players[pid]
                d = drivers[pid]
                ent = d.script[min(d.wp, len(d.script) - 1)]
                tgt = d._target(sim, ent, AR.weapon_stats(st["weapon"])
                                ["range"] * d.RANGE_FRAC)
                td = ("-" if tgt is None else
                      "%.0f" % math.hypot(tgt["x"] - st["x"],
                                          tgt["y"] - st["y"]))
                rows.append("%s(%d,%d)hp%d%s wp%d rc%d %s tgt%s los%d hold%d gap%d"
                            % (nick_of[pid][:6], st["x"], st["y"], st["hp"],
                               "DEAD" if st["dead"] else "    ", d.wp,
                               d._respawn_count, ent.get("do", "move"), td,
                               d._no_los, d._burst_hold, d._gap))
            print("  --- t=%2ds " % sec + " | ".join(rows))
    return sim, shots, kills, nick_of, hist, motion


def report(sim, shots, kills, nick_of, hist, motion):
    problems = []
    print("  shots %d   kills %d   phase=%s"
          % (len(shots), len(kills), sim.rules.phase))
    if not shots:
        print("  NO SHOTS AT ALL")
        return False
    first = shots[0][0] / T
    gaps = [(shots[i][0] - shots[i - 1][0]) / T for i in range(1, len(shots))]
    worst = max(gaps) if gaps else 0.0
    print("  first shot  %5.2fs   (gate: < %.2f)" % (first, GATE_FIRST_SHOT))
    print("  worst gap   %5.2fs   (gate: < %.2f)" % (worst, GATE_MAX_GAP))
    print("  shots/sec   " + " ".join("%3d" % v for v in hist))

    per = {}
    for _t, s in shots:
        per[nick_of.get(s, s)] = per.get(nick_of.get(s, s), 0) + 1
    print("  shots by    " + "  ".join("%s=%d" % kv for kv in sorted(per.items())))
    moving = True
    for pid in sorted(motion):
        m = motion[pid]
        dx, dy = m["maxx"] - m["minx"], m["maxy"] - m["miny"]
        nick = nick_of[pid]
        print("  move %-13s %4.0fpx  span %3.0fx%3.0fpx"
              % (nick[:13], m["distance"], dx, dy))
        if m["distance"] < 70.0 or max(dx, dy) < 40.0:
            moving = False
            problems.append("%s barely moved" % nick)

    print("  killfeed:")
    for t, k, v in kills:
        print("    %5.2fs  %-13s > %s" % (t / T, nick_of.get(k, k),
                                          nick_of.get(v, v)))
    sc = sim.rules.kills
    ipa = sum(sc.get(p, 0) for p, s in sim.players.items() if s["team"] == 0)
    krap = sum(sc.get(p, 0) for p, s in sim.players.items() if s["team"] == 1)
    print("  score       IPA %d - %d KRAP" % (ipa, krap))

    team_of = {nick_of[pid]: s["team"] for pid, s in sim.players.items()}
    for n, v in sorted(per.items()):
        if v < GATE_MIN_SHOTS:
            problems.append("%s barely participated (%d shots)" % (n, v))
    if ipa and krap and max(ipa, krap) / float(ipa + krap) > 0.7:
        problems.append("lopsided %d-%d" % (ipa, krap))
    if not krap or not ipa:
        problems.append("one team did not score")

    last = {"IPA": None, "KRAP": None}
    lull = 0.0
    for t, k, _v in kills:
        side = "IPA" if team_of.get(nick_of.get(k)) == 0 else "KRAP"
        if last[side] is not None:
            lull = max(lull, (t - last[side]) / T)
        last[side] = t
    print("  longest stretch without a score: %.2fs   (gate: < %.2f)"
          % (lull, GATE_MAX_SCORELULL))
    if lull > GATE_MAX_SCORELULL:
        problems.append("killfeed stalled %.2fs" % lull)
    if first >= GATE_FIRST_SHOT:
        problems.append("first shot too late")
    if worst >= GATE_MAX_GAP:
        problems.append("dry gap in the middle of the fight")
    if not kills:
        problems.append("nobody died")

    for p in problems:
        print("  FAIL " + p)
    print("  VERDICT     " + ("PASS" if not problems else "FAIL"))
    return not problems


def main():
    allok = True
    for seed in SEEDS:
        print("=" * 66)
        print("CHOREOGRAPHY DRY RUN  seed=%d" % seed)
        print("=" * 66)
        sim, shots, kills, nick_of, hist, motion = run(seed=seed)
        allok &= report(sim, shots, kills, nick_of, hist, motion)
    print("=" * 66)
    print("ALL SEEDS PASS" if allok else "SOME SEEDS FAILED - retune and re-run")
    print("=" * 66)
    return 0 if allok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_host.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Self-hosted KRAPNET server for Call of Acaristan.

This is the "host a game and give your friends the address" tool. A player
runs it (or the packaged EXE), it opens a port on their router, prints an
address, and their friends connect straight to it. No central server, no
account, no master.

    python tools/mp_host.py                       # host with defaults
    python tools/mp_host.py --name "Biribel's Server"
    python tools/mp_host.py --port 27020
    python tools/mp_host.py --no-forward          # skip UPnP/NAT-PMP
    python tools/mp_host.py --check               # diagnose, host nothing

How it works
------------
The hosted thing is a *lobby relay*, exactly like tools/mp_server.py: it
serves the server list and relays chat. It does NOT run the game. Two
people can connect to it and talk; they cannot yet play together. That
limit is honest and is called out in the startup banner, because selling
this as "play with your friends" would be a lie.

Getting reachable from the internet is the interesting part, and it is not
in our control:

  * If the router supports UPnP or NAT-PMP, the port is opened
    automatically and we print the public address.
  * If not, we still print the LAN address, and explain exactly what to
    forward by hand. Many routers simply have UPnP switched off.
  * Double NAT (ISP modem + own router) and CGNAT will defeat this no
    matter what we do; the tool says so rather than pretending.

Everything is stdlib-only so the packaged EXE stays small and has no
install-time surprises.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import shutil
import signal
import socketserver
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "src"))

from net import portmap, tcp_tunnel  # noqa: E402
from net import protocol as P  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from mp_server import (  # noqa: E402
    MasterHandler, MasterState, ThreadedTCPServer,
)

DEFAULT_PORT = 27015
DEFAULT_NAME = "Call of Acaristan -- hosted game"
DEFAULT_MAX_PLAYERS = 8

RULES_TEMPLATE = [
    "GAMEMODE:  Hosted lobby",
    "MAP:       (to be announced)",
    "RULES:     1. Be decent. This is the internet.",
    "           2. Cheating ruins it for everyone.",
    "           3. Host has the final say.",
]


def _c(text=""):
    sys.stdout.write(text + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()


def start_tunnel(port, timeout=25.0):
    """Use the same tested raw-TCP tunnel path as the arena."""
    endpoint, proc, provider = tcp_tunnel.start_tunnel(port, timeout)
    if endpoint:
        return provider, "%s:%d" % endpoint, proc
    _c("  Tunnel unavailable: " + tcp_tunnel.explain_error(provider))
    return None, None, None


def build_state(args):
    """Create the master state with exactly one row: this host's server."""
    state = MasterState(seed=False)
    state.register((args.name, 0, args.max_players, 0), RULES_TEMPLATE)
    return state


def firewall_hint():
    """A hint about the host firewall, a problem separate from NAT.

    On Windows the game EXE can be blocked by Defender Firewall. The
    listening socket still works locally, but inbound connections from
    outside get dropped. We cannot detect this reliably from here, so we
    print a note rather than pretending to know.
    """
    return ("If friends cannot connect, allow the executable through "
            "Windows Defender Firewall (private and public).")


def report_status(args, local):
    """Print network diagnostics without binding anything."""
    ext = portmap.public_ip()
    _c("  Public IP   : %s" % (ext if ext else "unknown (STUN blocked?)"))
    _c("  Behind NAT  : %s" % ("yes" if portmap.is_private(local) else "no"))
    locs = portmap._ssdp_discover(timeout=2.0)
    _c("  UPnP gateway: %s" % ("found" if locs else "none found"))
    _c("")
    _c("  Notes:")
    _c("   - " + firewall_hint())
    _c("   - Double NAT (modem + router) or carrier CGNAT cannot be fixed")
    _c("     from software. You would need a tunnel or a VPS.")


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Host a Call of Acaristan lobby and share the address")
    ap.add_argument("--name", default=DEFAULT_NAME,
                    help="server name friends will see")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PORT)
    ap.add_argument("--max-players", type=int, default=DEFAULT_MAX_PLAYERS)
    ap.add_argument("--no-forward", action="store_true",
                    help="do not attempt UPnP/NAT-PMP port forwarding")
    ap.add_argument("--tunnel", action="store_true",
                    help="get a public address via bore/ngrok, "
                         "so you never need to configure your router")
    ap.add_argument("--prefer-tunnel", action="store_true",
                    help="try the tunnel first, before UPnP")
    ap.add_argument("--no-discovery", action="store_true",
                    help="do not answer LAN discovery probes")
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
                    help="report network status and exit without hosting")
    ap.add_argument("-q", "--quiet", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    args.max_players = max(1, min(64, args.max_players))
    local = portmap.local_ip()

    _c("=" * 66)
    _c("  CALL OF ACARISTAN -- SELF-HOSTED LOBBY")
    _c("=" * 66)
    _c("  This hosts a LOBBY: server list + chat.")
    _c("  It does NOT run the game yet -- you can talk to friends here,")
    _c("  but you cannot play together yet. That is a separate project.")
    _c("")
    _c("  Server name : %s" % args.name)
    _c("  Port        : %d" % args.port)
    _c("  Max players : %d" % args.max_players)
    _c("  Your LAN IP : %s" % local)

    if args.check:
        _c("")
        report_status(args, local)
        return 0

    state = build_state(args)
    try:
        server = ThreadedTCPServer(("0.0.0.0", args.port), MasterHandler,
                                   state, verbose=not args.quiet)
    except OSError as exc:
        _c("")
        _c("  FAILED to bind port %d: %s" % (args.port, exc))
        _c("  Another program may be using it. Try --port 27020.")
        return 1

    stop_evt = threading.Event()
    if not args.no_discovery:
        from mp_server import run_discovery
        threading.Thread(target=run_discovery,
                         args=(P.DISCOVERY_PORT, args.port, stop_evt,
                               not args.quiet), daemon=True).start()

    _c("")
    _c("  Listening on 0.0.0.0:%d" % args.port)
    _c("")
    _c("-" * 66)

    forwarded = False
    tunnel_proc = None
    share = "%s:%d" % (local, args.port)

    if args.tunnel or args.prefer_tunnel:
        exe, hp, tunnel_proc = start_tunnel(args.port)
        if hp:
            share = hp
            forwarded = True
            _c("  Public address via %s: %s" % (exe, hp))
        elif not args.prefer_tunnel:
            _c("  Try reinstalling the game, or tools/download_bore.py for source runs.")
            _c("  Continuing with the normal method...")
    if not args.prefer_tunnel:
        if args.no_forward:
            _c("  Port forwarding skipped (--no-forward).")
        elif not tunnel_proc:
            _c("  Asking your router to open the port (UPnP, then NAT-PMP)...")
            result = portmap.open_port(
                args.port, args.port,
                description="Call of Acaristan (%s)" % args.name)
            if result.ok:
                forwarded = True
                _c("  Port forwarded via %s." % result.method)
                ext = result.external_ip or portmap.public_ip()
                if ext:
                    share = "%s:%d" % (ext, args.port)
            else:
                _c("  Could not forward the port automatically.")
                _c("  Reason: %s" % result.error)
                if result.guidance:
                    _c("  Fix: %s" % result.guidance)

    _c("")
    _c("  GIVE YOUR FRIENDS THIS ADDRESS:")
    _c("")
    _c("      %s" % share)
    _c("")
    if not forwarded:
        _c("  NOTE: that is your LAN address. Friends on the SAME wifi can")
        _c("        use it. Friends elsewhere need the port forwarded, or")
        _c("        they need a VPN/tunnel with you (Tailnet, ZeroTier, ngrok).")
        _c("  EASIEST: re-run with --tunnel and we do it for you.")
    else:
        _c("  Anyone on the internet can use that address while this")
        _c("  window stays open.")
    _c("")
    _c("  Friends do NOT need the game to chat. They can just run:")
    _c("      python tools/mp_join.py")
    _c("  and paste the address above.")
    _c("")
    _c("  " + firewall_hint())
    _c("")
    _c("-" * 66)
    _c("  Press Ctrl+C to stop hosting.")
    _c("-" * 66)

    def _sig(_signum, _frame):
        stop_evt.set()
        server.stopping = True
        threading.Thread(target=server.shutdown, daemon=True).start()

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _sig)
    try:
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _sig)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, OSError):
        pass

    seen = {"n": -1, "t": 0.0}

    def _reporter():
        """Periodically tell the host how many people are actually here."""
        while not stop_evt.is_set():
            time.sleep(2.0)
            try:
                count = len(state.clients)
            except Exception:
                continue
            now = time.time()
            if count != seen["n"] or now - seen["t"] > 30:
                seen["n"] = count
                seen["t"] = now
                if not args.quiet:
                    _c("  [%s] %d connected" % (time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), count))

    threading.Thread(target=_reporter, daemon=True).start()

    try:
        server.serve_forever(poll_interval=0.2)
    finally:
        stop_evt.set()
        server.server_close()
        # The tunnel is a child process; leaving it running would keep our
        # local port exposed to the internet after we stop hosting. That is
        # a security problem, not just a stray handle, so it always dies
        # with us -- including on Ctrl+C and on an unhandled exception.
        if tunnel_proc is not None:
            tcp_tunnel.stop_process(tunnel_proc)
            _c("  Tunnel closed.")
        _c("")
        _c("  Hosting stopped.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_host_main.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""PyInstaller entry point for the self-hosted lobby EXE.

Kept as a separate file from mp_host.py so the console (not --windowed) is
used: a host NEEDS to see the address to share it, the connection count, and
any firewall/port-forwarding instructions. A silent GUI host would be worse
than useless.

Build with tools/build_host_exe.bat.
"""

import os
import sys

# mp_host.py lives next to this file and does its own sys.path setup for src/
# and tools/, so importing it is all that is needed.
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

import mp_host  # noqa: E402

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # When frozen, argparse must not try to read PyInstaller's own argv.
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if getattr(sys, "frozen", False) else sys.argv[1:]
    raise SystemExit(mp_host.main(argv))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_join.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Join a friend's Call of Acaristan lobby and chat. No game required.

    python tools/mp_join.py                  # asks for the address
    python tools/mp_join.py 1.2.3.4:27015   # or pass it straight in

This exists because the hard part of "test it with a friend" was never the
networking -- it was that your friend had to already own the game, install
Python, and know what a CONNECT box is. They do not. So this asks for one
thing (the address you texted them) and drops them into the chat.

The game itself offers the same chat under Multiplayer. This is the
zero-friction path for anyone who just wants to talk.
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
import threading
import time

# Chat must appear line-by-line even when stdout is a pipe or a log file.
# Python block-buffers redirected output, so without this a friend running
# the EXE with output captured would see nothing until the buffer filled.
try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)
except AttributeError:
    pass  # very old Python; nothing to do

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "src"))

from net import protocol as P  # noqa: E402
from net.client import (  # noqa: E402
    MPRelayClient, register_chat_sink,
    ST_CONNECTING, ST_ERROR, ST_ONLINE,
)

LOCK = threading.Lock()
LINES = []          # (who, text) newest last
SEEN = set()        # dedupe so a backfilled line is not reprinted
MAXKEEP = 400


def sink(msg):
    """Chat sink. Runs on the client's worker thread, so guard the list."""
    who = msg.get("user", "?")
    text = msg.get("text", "")
    with LOCK:
        key = (who, text)
        if key in SEEN:
            return
        SEEN.add(key)
        LINES.append((who, text))
        if len(LINES) > MAXKEEP:
            del LINES[0:len(LINES) - MAXKEEP]


def parse_addr(text):
    """Accept 'host', 'host:port', or a pasted ngrok/url style string.

    Returns (host, port) or None. Forgiving here matters: your friend will
    paste whatever you sent them, stray slash and scheme included.
    """
    t = (text or "").strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    if not t:
        return None
    for pre in ("tcp://", "http://", "https://"):
        if t.lower().startswith(pre):
            t = t[len(pre):]
    t = t.rstrip("/")
    for sep in ("?", "#", "/"):
        if sep in t:
            t = t.split(sep, 1)[0]
    port = P.DEFAULT_MASTER_PORT
    if t.count(":") == 1:
        h, _, p = t.partition(":")
        if p.isdigit() and 1 <= int(p) <= 65535:
            t, port = h, int(p)
    if not t or " " in t or not all(c.isalnum() or c in ".-" for c in t):
        return None
    return t, port


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Join a Call of Acaristan lobby and chat")
    ap.add_argument("address", nargs="?", default=None,
                    help="host or host:port (skips the prompt)")
    ap.add_argument("--name", default=None, help="your display name")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    addr = args.address
    if not addr:
        print("=" * 58)
        print("  CALL OF ACARISTAN -- JOIN A FRIEND'S LOBBY")
        print("=" * 58)
        print("")
        print("  Your friend should have sent you an address that")
        print("  looks like  1.2.3.4:27015")
        print("")
        try:
            addr = input("  Paste it here: ").strip()
        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
            print("")
            return 1

    parsed = parse_addr(addr)
    if not parsed:
        print("")
        print("  That does not look like an address.")
        print("  It should look like  1.2.3.4:27015  or just  1.2.3.4")
        print("")
        return 1
    host, port = parsed

    nick = args.name
    if not nick:
        default = (os.environ.get("USERNAME")
                   or os.environ.get("USER") or "friend")
        try:
            nick = input("  Your name [%s]: " % default).strip() or default
        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
            nick = default

    client = MPRelayClient(host=host, port=port, nickname=nick)
    # Chat arrives on the client's worker thread; sink() is lock-guarded.
    register_chat_sink(sink)
    client.start()

    print("")
    print("  Connecting to %s:%d as %s ..." % (host, port, nick))
    print("  Type a message and press Enter to send it.")
    print("  Ctrl+C to leave.")
    print("")

    stop = threading.Event()

    # Input() blocks, so reading it on a worker keeps incoming chat
    # scrolling while you are half-way through typing a reply.
    def _reader():
        while not stop.is_set():
            try:
                line = input("")
            except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
                stop.set()
                return
            if stop.is_set():
                return
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            if line.lower() in ("/quit", "/exit", "/q"):
                stop.set()
                return
            try:
                client.send_chat(line)
                # Type-and-quit is normal for a friend who fires off a last
                # line and closes the window; don't let that message vanish.
                client.flush(timeout=1.0)
            except Exception as exc:
                print("  Could not send: %s" % exc)

    threading.Thread(target=_reader, daemon=True).start()

    printed = 0
    last_status = None
    try:
        while not stop.is_set():
            time.sleep(0.1)
            status, error, _servers, _nick = client.state()
            if status != last_status:
                last_status = status
                if status == ST_ONLINE:
                    print("  [connected] say something")
                elif status == ST_ERROR and error:
                    print("  [problem] %s" % error)
                elif status == ST_CONNECTING:
                    print("  [connecting]")
            with LOCK:
                batch = LINES[printed:]
                printed = len(LINES)
            for who, text in batch:
                print("  <%s> %s" % (who, text))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        stop.set()
        client.flush(timeout=1.0)
        client.stop()

    print("")
    print("  Disconnected.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_match.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Play a real multiplayer arena match. This is the whole stack in one file.

    python tools/mp_match.py --host                    # you host
    python tools/mp_match.py --join 192.168.1.42:27015  # friend joins
    python tools/mp_match.py --host --tunnel           # public, no router setup

Controls: WASD to move, mouse to aim, left click (hold) to fire, Esc to quit.

This exists because steps 1-3 were proven by headless tests, and a headless
test cannot tell you whether the game is any fun. Running the real renderer
against the real simulation over a real socket is the only way to find the
problems that only appear when all three are wired together at once: input
latency you can feel, camera lag, a fire rate that feels wrong.

It is also the fastest way to play with a friend before the in-game menu
exists, and it uses the same modules the game will, so nothing here is
throwaway.
"""
import argparse
import math
import os
import select
import socket
import sys
import threading
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "src"))

import pygame  # noqa: E402

from net import protocol as P  # noqa: E402
from net.match import Fanout, MatchSession, TICK_RATE  # noqa: E402
from missions import arena as AR  # noqa: E402
from ui.arena_view import ArenaView  # noqa: E402

VIEW_W, VIEW_H = 1000, 700
STEP = 1.0 / TICK_RATE
SCORE_LIMIT = 15


class Wire(object):
    """Newline-JSON framing over a socket, shared by host and client.

    Reuses the relay lobby's framing exactly rather than inventing a second
    transport; anything that speaks the lobby can speak this.
    """

    def __init__(self, sock):
        self.sock = sock
        self.out = b""
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    # Named _send, not send, to match MPRelayClient: that is the contract
    # MatchSession._send() looks for. Naming it `send` meant the attribute
    # lookup failed, every snapshot was silently dropped, and the client
    # rendered an empty world -- which reads like a rendering bug rather
    # than a missing underscore.
    def _send(self, obj):
        with self.lock:
            self.out += P.encode(obj)
            if len(self.out) > 16384:
                self.flush()

    def flush(self):
        with self.lock:
            if not self.out:
                return
            data, self.out = self.out, b""
        try:
            self.sock.sendall(data)
        except OSError:
            pass


def aim_degrees(mouse, player_xy, cam_x, cam_y):
    """Angle from the player toward the mouse, in degrees.

    The mouse is screen-space, so it is converted back into world space
    first. Getting this wrong makes everyone shoot in a direction that
    looks right on their own screen and is nonsense to everybody else.
    """
    wx, wy = mouse[0] + cam_x, mouse[1] + cam_y
    return math.degrees(math.atan2(wy - player_xy[1],
                                   wx - player_xy[0])) % 360.0


def parse_addr(text):
    """'host', 'host:port', or a pasted cloudflared/ngrok address."""
    t = (text or "").strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    for pre in ("tcp://", "http://", "https://"):
        if t.lower().startswith(pre):
            t = t[len(pre):]
    t = t.rstrip("/")
    for sep in ("?", "#", "/"):
        if sep in t:
            t = t.split(sep, 1)[0]
    port = 27015
    if t.count(":") == 1:
        h, _, p = t.partition(":")
        if p.isdigit() and 1 <= int(p) <= 65535:
            t, port = h, int(p)
    return t or "127.0.0.1", port


def _open_display():
    screen = pygame.display.set_mode((VIEW_W, VIEW_H))
    pygame.display.set_caption("ACARISTAN -- ARENA")
    return screen


class Peer(object):
    """One connected client and the player slot it owns.

    Keeping the read buffer and the assigned id together on the connection
    is what stops the classic roster bug: assigning a player id at accept
    time but freeing it somewhere else, so a late joiner inherits a slot
    whose previous owner is still sending input.
    """

    def __init__(self, sock, addr, player_id):
        self.sock = sock
        self.addr = addr
        self.player_id = player_id
        self.wire = Wire(sock)
        self.buf = b""

    def close(self):
        try:
            self.sock.close()
        except OSError:
            pass


def run_host(args, screen):
    """Bind, accept a roster of players, then simulate and render at 60 Hz.

    Accepting continues for the whole match, not just at the start, so a
    friend who is late still gets a slot instead of being told the match
    already began. That is what makes "invite three people" work.
    """
    srv = socket.socket()
    srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    srv.bind(("0.0.0.0", args.port))
    srv.listen(args.players)
    srv.setblocking(False)
    local_ip = socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname())
    print("Hosting %s on port %d.  Local: %s:%d"
          % (args.map, args.port, local_ip, args.port))
    print("Up to %d players.  Waiting for someone to join..." % args.players)

    # Slot 0 is always the host's own player, so remote players start at 1
    # and the local id stays a constant.
    sess = MatchSession(Fanout(lambda: peers), is_host=True, local_id=0)
    sim = AR.ArenaSim(sess, AR.ARENAS[args.map], score_limit=args.score,
                      map_name=args.map)
    sim.add_player(0, "HOST")
    view = ArenaView(args.map)

    peers = []
    started = False
    clock = pygame.time.Clock()
    acc = 0.0
    running = True
    tracer = None
    tracer_t = 0.0
    while running:
        dt = clock.tick(60) / 1000.0
        for ev in pygame.event.get():
            if ev.type == pygame.QUIT:
                running = False
            elif ev.type == pygame.KEYDOWN and ev.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
                running = False
        keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
        mx, my = pygame.mouse.get_pos()
        firing = pygame.mouse.get_pressed()[0]

        # ── accept new players ──
        # A full lobby must not spin on accept(); check the count first.
        if len(peers) < args.players - 1:
            try:
                conn, addr = srv.accept()
            except (BlockingIOError, OSError):
                conn = None
            if conn is not None:
                conn.setblocking(False)
                conn.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
                # Lowest free slot, so ids stay small and stable.
                used = set(p.player_id for p in peers)
                pid = next(i for i in range(1, args.players) if i not in used)
                peers.append(Peer(conn, addr, pid))
                sim.add_player(pid, "P%d" % pid)
                print("P%d joined from %s  (%d/%d)"
                      % (pid, addr[0], len(peers) + 1, args.players))
                if not started:
                    started = True
                    print("Match started.")

        # ── read every client ──
        # select() rather than a thread per peer: a thread each would put
        # shared simulation state behind locks for no benefit, since all the
        # real work has to happen on this one loop anyway.
        if peers:
            try:
                ready, _, _ = select.select([p.sock for p in peers], [], [], 0)
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                ready = []
            for sock in ready:
                peer = next((p for p in peers if p.sock is sock), None)
                if peer is None:
                    continue
                try:
                    chunk = sock.recv(65536)
                except (BlockingIOError, OSError):
                    continue
                if chunk == b"":
                    print("P%d left." % peer.player_id)
                    sim.remove_player(peer.player_id)
                    peer.close()
                    peers.remove(peer)
                    continue
                peer.buf += chunk
                if len(peer.buf) > 1 << 20:
                    # A peer streaming without newlines must not eat RAM.
                    sim.remove_player(peer.player_id)
                    peer.close()
                    peers.remove(peer)
                    continue
                while b"\n" in peer.buf:
                    line, peer.buf = peer.buf.split(b"\n", 1)
                    if not line.strip():
                        continue
                    # Hand the RAW dict to _accept_input and let it do the
                    # validating. Parsing here first strips the "t" field, and the
                    # validation in _accept_input then rejects the packet as "not an
                    # input" -- so every remote player's input was silently dropped
                    # while local play worked fine.
                    raw = P.decode(line)
                    if isinstance(raw, dict):
                            sess._accept_input(raw, peer_id=peer.player_id)

        # The host's own player is driven from its keyboard, exactly like a
        # remote one is driven from the network -- one code path, so local
        # and remote play can never diverge.
        me = sim.players[0]
        ax, ay = local_axes(keys)
        buttons = P.F_FIRING if firing else 0
        sess._accept_input(
            {"t": P.T_INPUT, "q": sim.tick, "mx": ax, "my": ay,
             "a": aim_degrees((mx, my), (me["x"], me["y"]),
                              view.cam_x, view.cam_y), "b": buttons},
            peer_id=0)

        acc += min(dt, 0.1)
        steps = 0
        while acc >= STEP and steps < 5:
            sim.step()
            if sim.last_shot:
                tracer = sim.last_shot
                tracer_t = time.time()
            acc -= STEP
            steps += 1

        world = dict((e[0], e) for e in sess.world)
        view.draw(screen, world, 0, sim.scoreboard())
        _draw_lobby(screen, len(peers) + 1, args.players)
        if tracer and time.time() - tracer_t < 0.07:
            _draw_tracer(screen, view, tracer)
        if sim.finished:
            _draw_banner(screen, sim.winner)
        pygame.display.flip()

    srv.close()
    for peer in peers:
        peer.close()


def _draw_lobby(screen, count, maximum):
    """Show the roster size. Without this, a friend whose connection failed
    silently has no way to tell joining apart from being ignored."""
    try:
        font = pygame.font.Font(None, 20)
        surf = font.render("PLAYERS %d/%d" % (count, maximum), True,
                           (170, 180, 200))
    except Exception:
        return
    screen.blit(surf, (screen.get_width() - surf.get_width() - 10, 26))


def _draw_tracer(screen, view, shot):
    x, y, ang, dist = shot
    rad = math.radians(ang)
    sx = int(x - view.cam_x)
    sy = int(y - view.cam_y)
    pygame.draw.line(screen, (255, 226, 150), (sx, sy),
                     (sx + math.cos(rad) * dist,
                      sy + math.sin(rad) * dist), 2)


def _draw_banner(screen, winner):
    try:
        font = pygame.font.Font(None, 64)
        surf = font.render("MATCH OVER", True, (255, 210, 90))
    except Exception:
        return
    screen.blit(surf, (screen.get_width() // 2 - surf.get_width() // 2, 60))


def local_axes(keys):
    """WASD/arrows -> (-1..1, -1..1). """
    dx = dy = 0
    if keys[pygame.K_w] or keys[pygame.K_UP]:
        dy -= 1
    if keys[pygame.K_s] or keys[pygame.K_DOWN]:
        dy += 1
    if keys[pygame.K_a] or keys[pygame.K_LEFT]:
        dx -= 1
    if keys[pygame.K_d] or keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]:
        dx += 1
    return dx, dy
def run_client(args, screen):
    """Connect, send input at 60 Hz, draw interpolated snapshots."""
    host, port = parse_addr(args.join)
    sock = socket.socket()
    sock.connect((host, port))
    sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
    sock.setblocking(False)
    print("Connected to %s:%d.  WASD to move, mouse to aim, hold LMB to fire."
          % (host, port))

    wire = Wire(sock)
    sess = MatchSession(wire, is_host=False, local_id=0)
    view = ArenaView(args.map)
    # Announce as a match client before anything else. The in-game host
    # (ui/match_screen.py) holds every accepted connection unverified until
    # this arrives, so without it an in-game host would drop this tool.
    wire._send(P.make_join_match(args.map))
    wire.flush()

    buf = b""
    seq = 0
    clock = pygame.time.Clock()
    running = True
    while running:
        for ev in pygame.event.get():
            if ev.type == pygame.QUIT:
                running = False
            elif ev.type == pygame.KEYDOWN and ev.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
                running = False
        clock.tick(60)
        keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
        mx, my = pygame.mouse.get_pos()
        firing = pygame.mouse.get_pressed()[0]

        try:
            chunk = sock.recv(65536)
            if chunk == b"":
                print("Host closed the connection.")
                running = False
            elif chunk:
                buf += chunk
                while b"\n" in buf:
                    line, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
                    if not line.strip():
                        continue
                    msg = P.parse_snapshot(P.decode(line))
                    if msg is not None:
                        sess._accept_snapshot(P.make_snapshot(*msg))
                        # The only clock both sides share is the host's tick
                        # counter, so the client tracks the newest snapshot
                        # it has rather than counting its own frames. Leaving
                        # sess.tick at 0 would leave the interpolation buffer
                        # permanently behind and the world frozen.
                        sess.tick = msg[0]
        except (BlockingIOError, OSError):
            pass

        world = sess.sample_world() or {}
        me = world.get(0)
        if me is not None:
            # Send input only once we actually know where we are. Sending
            # before the first snapshot would move the host's idea of us
            # from a guessed origin, which is how players end up stuck
            # inside geometry on join.
            ax, ay = local_axes(keys)
            wire._send({"t": P.T_INPUT, "q": seq,
                       "mx": ax, "my": ay,
                       "a": aim_degrees((mx, my), (me[2], me[3]),
                                        view.cam_x, view.cam_y),
                       "b": P.F_FIRING if firing else 0})
            seq = (seq + 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        wire.flush()

        view.draw(screen, world, 0, ())
        pygame.display.flip()

    sock.close()


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Play an arena match")
    g = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    g.add_argument("--host", action="store_true", help="host the match")
    g.add_argument("--join", help="host or host:port to join")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=27015)
    ap.add_argument("--map", default="yard", choices=sorted(AR.ARENAS))
    ap.add_argument("--players", type=int, default=4,
                    help="max players in the match, host included (2-8)")
    ap.add_argument("--score", type=int, default=SCORE_LIMIT,
                    help="kills to win")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.players = max(2, min(8, args.players))
    args.score = max(1, min(99, args.score))

    pygame.init()
    screen = _open_display()
    try:
        if args.host:
            run_host(args, screen)
        else:
            run_client(args, screen)
    finally:
        pygame.quit()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# tools\mp_remaster.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Re-master audio only: reuse the kept premix.wav, re-run normalise + mux.

Usage: python tools/mp_remaster.py <assembler_workdir>
    <assembler_workdir> = a mp_trailer_assemble.py --keep-stems run dir
    containing premix.wav + silent_master.mp4.
"""
import shutil, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import mp_trailer_assemble as A

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    sys.exit("usage: python tools/mp_remaster.py <assembler_workdir>  "
             "(a mp_trailer_assemble.py --keep-stems run with premix.wav "
             "+ silent_master.mp4)")
SRC = Path(sys.argv[1])
SRC_PREMIX = SRC / "premix.wav"
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mp_remaster_"))
premix = work / "premix.wav"
shutil.copy2(SRC_PREMIX, premix)

audio = A.normalise(work, premix)

A.run([A.FFMPEG, "-y", "-i", SRC / "silent_master.mp4",
       "-i", audio, "-map", "0:v", "-map", "1:a",
       "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k",
       "-movflags", "+faststart", str(A.OUT_FINAL)],
      f"mux -> {A.OUT_FINAL.name}")
shutil.copy2(A.OUT_FINAL, A.OUT_PROJECT)
d = A.dur_of(A.OUT_FINAL)
print(f"REMASTERED {A.OUT_FINAL} {d:.2f}s {A.OUT_FINAL.stat().st_size/1e6:.1f} MB")
sys.stdout.flush()
import os
os._exit(0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# tools\mp_server.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------

"""Standalone KRAPNET master server for Call of Acaristan.

Run it next to the game (or on a VPS / LAN box):

    python tools/mp_server.py                       # 127.0.0.1:27015
    python tools/mp_server.py --host 0.0.0.0        # reachable on the LAN
    python tools/mp_server.py --port 27020

What it does
------------
  * Accepts client connections on TCP and answers ``query`` packets with the
    current server list, the way a Steam/Source master server does.
  * Relays ``chat`` lines to every connected client.
  * Optionally advertises itself on UDP 27016 so LAN clients can find it
    with no configuration (see ``--no-discovery`` to disable).

A note on scope: this is a *lobby relay*, not a game server. It carries the
server list and the global chat channel and nothing else -- no simulation, no
player state, no gameplay traffic. Gameplay lives in ARENA MATCH, on its own
socket, and does not pass through here at all (see the ports table in
docs/KRAPNET_MULTIPLAYER.md for why).

There are no accounts, but there are limits: a chat rate floor, a per-name
registration interval, a cap on live rows and a cap on concurrent clients.
Those contain a flood; they do not authenticate anybody. Anyone can still
claim any name.

Everything here is stdlib-only and deliberately boring: a thread per client,
a dict of rows, newline-delimited JSON.
"""

import argparse
import os
import signal

from net import protocol as P  # noqa: E402

# The seeded row set: the servers the master reports when no real game
# server has registered, so a fresh install still has something to browse.
SEED_SERVERS = [
    ("Vasile's Cigarette Break", 1, 4, 12),
    ("Biribel's Safe House (PASS: 742)", 0, 2, 67),
    ("MAG Recruitment Center", 24, 32, 88),
    ("Krapistan #1 Official", 0, 64, 350),
    ("noobs only pls", 3, 10, 156),
    ("[24/7] OIL RIG EXPLOSION SIM", 12, 16, 78),
    ("MR.BEAST GIVING AWAY CIGARETTES", 99, 100, 45),
    ("yo mama's basement", 1, 2, 4),
]

SEED_RULES = {
    "Vasile's Cigarette Break": [
        "GAMEMODE:  Cigarette Break",
        "MAP:       Alleyway",
        "RULES:     Nobody is actually on a break.",
    ],
    "MAG Recruitment Center": [
        "GAMEMODE:  Recruitment",
        "MAP:       Recruitment Hall",
        "RULES:     Sign the sheet. Then sign up.",
    ],
    "Krapistan #1 Official": [
        "GAMEMODE:  Official Business",
        "MAP:       Krapistan City",
        "RULES:     Read the rules. They are the rules.",
    ],
}

SERVER_TTL = 15.0
MAX_MSG = 1 << 20

# ── Abuse limits ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This master has no accounts and no passwords, which is a deliberate choice
# (paste an address, play) but it does NOT mean "unlimited". Without these a
# single client can flood every connected player's chat panel, publish
# thousands of fake rows to replace the real list, or open connections until
# the master runs out of threads. Each limit below is a floor a human cannot
# hit by accident and a script trips in seconds.
#
# What this is NOT: authentication. Anyone can still claim any name and any
# row. These bounds contain annoyance; they do not establish identity. See
# "Known limitations" in docs/KRAPNET_MULTIPLAYER.md.
CHAT_MIN_GAP = 0.4          # seconds between one client's chat lines
CHAT_BURST = 5             # ...but a burst of N is allowed back to back
CHAT_WINDOW = 10.0         # the burst is refilled over this many seconds
# Registration is how a row gets into everyone's browser, so it is the most
# abusable verb here. One row per name per interval is generous for a host
# re-registering its 15s TTL and impossible to spam with.
REGISTER_MIN_GAP = 2.0
REGISTER_MAX_NAMES = 64    # distinct live rows before further ones are refused
MAX_CLIENTS = 128          # concurrent sockets before new ones are refused



class TokenGate(object):
    """A token bucket with a floor, for one client.

    The floor is the part that matters for chat: a plain "N per second" limit
    punishes a fast typist exactly when they are most worth listening to, so a
    single line is always allowed through after ``gap`` seconds, while a burst
    of ``burst`` is allowed back to back and then refills at one per ``gap``.
    A human sending three quick lines is untouched; a script sending three
    hundred is cut off immediately.
    """

    def __init__(self, gap, burst):
        self.gap = max(0.0, float(gap))
        self.burst = max(1, int(burst))
        self.tokens = float(self.burst)
        self.last = time.monotonic()

    def allow(self):
        now = time.monotonic()
        self.tokens = min(float(self.burst),
                          self.tokens + (now - self.last) / max(self.gap, 1e-6))
        self.last = now
        if self.tokens >= 1.0:
            self.tokens -= 1.0
            return True
        return False


class MasterState(object):
    """Shared, lock-guarded state for one master process."""

    def __init__(self, seed=True):
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        # name -> {"name","current","max","ping","rules","seen"}
        self.servers = {}
        # conn -> {"id","name","sock"}
        self.clients = {}
        self.chat_log = []
        self.next_id = 1
        self.started = time.time()
        self.msg_counts = {}
        # Name -> monotonic time of its last accepted register. A gate per
        # NAME rather than per connection, because the abuse is "publish many
        # rows", and one socket could otherwise rename itself per line.
        self.register_seen = {}
        if seed:
            now = time.monotonic()
            for name, cur, mx, ping in SEED_SERVERS:
                self.servers[name] = {
                    "name": name,
                    "current": cur,
                    "max": mx,
                    "ping": ping,
                    "rules": SEED_RULES.get(name, []),
                    "seen": now,
                }

    def client_count(self):
        with self.lock:
            return len(self.clients)

    def may_register(self, name):
        """True if *name* may publish a row now. Records the attempt either way.

        The timestamp is recorded on every attempt, accepted or not, so a
        client that keeps hammering is slowed to one attempt per interval
        instead of one per round trip.
        """
        now = time.monotonic()
        with self.lock:
            live = len(self.servers)
            if live >= REGISTER_MAX_NAMES and name not in self.servers:
                return False, "server list is full (%d rows)" % live
            last = self.register_seen.get(name)
            if last is not None and now - last < REGISTER_MIN_GAP:
                return False, "registering too often; retry in %.1fs" % (
                    REGISTER_MIN_GAP - (now - last))
            self.register_seen[name] = now
            if len(self.register_seen) > 512:
                # Bound the bookkeeping, not the rows: an attacker must not be
                # able to grow this dict forever with names they never use.
                cutoff = now - REGISTER_MIN_GAP
                self.register_seen = dict(
                    (n, t) for n, t in self.register_seen.items() if t >= cutoff)
            return True, ""

    def register(self, row, rules=None):
        name, cur, mx, ping = row
        with self.lock:
            self.servers[name] = {
                "name": name,
                "current": cur,
                "max": mx,
                "ping": ping,
                "rules": list(rules or []),
                "seen": time.monotonic(),
            }
            return name

    def sweep(self):
        """Drop rows that stopped re-registering. Returns the dropped names."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        with self.lock:
            dead = [n for n, r in self.servers.items()
                    if now - r["seen"] > SERVER_TTL]
            for n in dead:
                del self.servers[n]
            return dead

    def list_payload(self):
        """Build the ``servers`` body: rows plus a rules side-table."""
        with self.lock:
            rows = [[r["name"], r["current"], r["max"], r["ping"]]
                    for r in sorted(self.servers.values(), key=lambda r: r["name"])]
            rules = dict((r["name"], r["rules"]) for r in self.servers.values())
        return rows, rules

    def add_chat(self, user, text, color):
        entry = {"user": user, "text": text, "color": color, "ts": time.time()}
        with self.lock:
            self.chat_log.append(entry)
            if len(self.chat_log) > 200:
                del self.chat_log[:-200]
        return entry

    def recent_chat(self, n=25):
        with self.lock:
            return list(self.chat_log[-n:])

    def add_client(self, conn, name):
        with self.lock:
            cid = self.next_id
            self.next_id += 1
            self.clients[conn] = {"id": cid, "name": name, "sock": conn}
            return cid

    def remove_client(self, conn):
        with self.lock:
            self.clients.pop(conn, None)

    def broadcast(self, obj, exclude=None):
        """Send one message to every client. Individual failures are dropped."""
        payload = P.encode(obj)
        with self.lock:
            targets = [(c, d["sock"]) for c, d in self.clients.items()
                       if c is not exclude]
        dead = []
        for conn, sock in targets:
            try:
                sock.sendall(payload)
            except OSError:
                dead.append(conn)
        for conn in dead:
            self.remove_client(conn)



class MasterHandler(socketserver.BaseRequestHandler):
    """One thread per connected client (via ThreadingTCPServer)."""

    def setup(self):
        self.state = self.server.state
        self.request.settimeout(0.5)
        self.buf = b""
        self.alive = True
        self.cid = None
        self.name = "anon"
        # Per-connection limits. Held here rather than in MasterState because
        # they are about THIS socket, and sharing them across clients would
        # mean one flood throttles everybody.
        self.chat_gate = TokenGate(CHAT_MIN_GAP, CHAT_BURST)
        self.spam_warned = False

    def handle(self):
        sock = self.request
        # Connection cap, checked before the client is registered so a refused
        # socket never appears in the broadcast set or the thread pool.
        if self.state.client_count() >= MAX_CLIENTS:
            self.send({"t": P.T_ERROR,
                       "text": "master is full (%d clients); try again later"
                               % MAX_CLIENTS})
            return
        self.cid = self.state.add_client(sock, self.name)
        self.log("client #%d connected from %s" % (
            self.cid, self.client_address[0]))
        self.send({"t": P.T_WELCOME, "name": self.name, "id": self.cid,
                   "proto": P.PROTO_VERSION,
                   "uptime": int(time.time() - self.state.started)})
        # Backfill recent chat so a joiner is not staring at an empty panel.
        for entry in self.state.recent_chat():
            self.send({"t": P.T_CHAT, "user": entry["user"],
                       "text": entry["text"], "color": entry["color"]})
        self.send_servers()
        try:
            while self.alive and not self.server.stopping:
                try:
                    chunk = sock.recv(4096)
                except socket.timeout:
                    continue
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not chunk:
                    break
                self.buf += chunk
                if len(self.buf) > MAX_MSG:
                    self.log("client #%d exceeded max buffer; dropping" % self.cid)
                    break
                while b"\n" in self.buf:
                    line, self.buf = self.buf.split(b"\n", 1)
                    line = line.strip()
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    msg = P.decode(line)
                    if msg:
                        self.on_message(msg)
                    else:
                        self.log("client #%d sent malformed JSON" % self.cid)
        finally:
            self.state.remove_client(sock)
            self.log("client #%d disconnected" % self.cid)

    def log(self, fmt, *a):
        if self.server.verbose:
            sys.stderr.write("[master] " + (fmt % a if a else fmt) + "\n")
            sys.stderr.flush()

    def send(self, obj):
        try:
            self.request.sendall(P.encode(obj))
            return True
        except OSError:
            self.alive = False
            return False

    def send_servers(self):
        rows, rules = self.state.list_payload()
        self.send({"t": P.T_SERVERS, "servers": rows, "rules": rules})

    def on_message(self, msg):
        kind = msg.get("t")
        self.state.msg_counts[kind] = self.state.msg_counts.get(kind, 0) + 1
        if kind == P.T_HELLO:
            name = msg.get("user")
            if isinstance(name, str) and name.strip():
                self.name = name.strip()[:32]
            if msg.get("proto") != P.PROTO_VERSION:
                self.send({"t": P.T_ERROR,
                           "text": "protocol mismatch; update the game"})
            # Re-send welcome now that we know who this is, so the client
            # can adopt the sanitised name (the first welcome still said
            # "anon" because it was sent before HELLO was read).
            self.send({"t": P.T_WELCOME, "name": self.name, "id": self.cid,
                       "proto": P.PROTO_VERSION})
            return
        if kind == P.T_QUERY:
            self.send_servers()
            return
        if kind == P.T_CHAT:
            text = msg.get("text")
            if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
                return
            # Throttle before relaying, not after: the cost of a flood is
            # paid by every OTHER client receiving it, so the gate has to sit
            # on the broadcast path. Warned once, because a client that is
            # merely typing fast should be corrected, not disconnected.
            if not self.chat_gate.allow():
                if not self.spam_warned:
                    self.spam_warned = True
                    # SOFT: this client is being throttled, not disconnected.
                    # A hard error here would make the client's relay session
                    # drop -- losing its server list and chat -- for having a
                    # fast typist.
                    self.send(P.make_error("sending too fast; slow down",
                                           soft=True))
                return
            text = P.sanitize_chat(text) or ""
            if not text:
                return
            entry = self.state.add_chat(self.name, text, P.color_for(self.name))
            self.state.broadcast({"t": P.T_CHAT, "user": entry["user"],
                                   "text": entry["text"],
                                   "color": entry["color"]})
            self.log("chat <%s> %s" % (self.name, text))
            return
        if kind == P.T_REGISTER:
            row = P.normalize_row(msg.get("row"))
            if row is None:
                self.send({"t": P.T_ERROR, "text": "bad register row"})
                return
            # Rules are the one register field with no bound in normalize_row,
            # so bound it here. Without this a single register can push
            # megabytes into the payload every client parses and draws in a
            # hover tooltip.
            rules = msg.get("rules")
            rules = [str(r)[:64] for r in rules[:16]] \
                if isinstance(rules, list) else []
            allowed, why = self.state.may_register(row[0])
            if not allowed:
                # Soft, for the same reason as the chat throttle: a host that
                # re-registers faster than the interval is misconfigured, not
                # malicious, and dropping its whole session over it would look
                # like the master had gone down.
                self.send(P.make_error(why, soft=True))
                self.log("refused register %r: %s" % (row[0], why))
                return
            self.state.register(row, rules)
            # A refused client may be mid-refresh and want a corrected list.
            self.send_servers()
            self.log("registered %r" % (row[0],))
            return
        if kind == P.T_BYE:
            self.alive = False
            return


class ThreadedTCPServer(socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer):
    """Threaded, reusable-address TCP server.

    allow_reuse_address matters on Windows: without it a restart trips over
    TIME_WAIT on the listening port and the server refuses to start.
    """

    allow_reuse_address = True
    daemon_threads = True

    def __init__(self, addr, handler, state, verbose=False):
        self.state = state
        self.verbose = verbose
        self.stopping = False
        socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer.__init__(self, addr, handler)

    def server_bind(self):
        self.socket.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
        socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer.server_bind(self)



def run_discovery(port, tcp_port, stop_evt, verbose=False):
    """Answer LAN discovery probes so clients need no configuration.

    A client broadcasts DISCOVERY_MAGIC to UDP ``port``; we reply with
    DISCOVERY_REPLY plus the TCP port to use. Windows usually prompts once
    for firewall permission on this socket, which is the intended UX.
    """
    try:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_BROADCAST, 1)
        sock.bind(("", port))
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[master] discovery disabled (%s)\n" % exc)
        return
    sys.stderr.write("[master] discovery beacon on udp/%d\n" % port)
    sys.stderr.flush()
    sock.settimeout(0.5)
    while not stop_evt.is_set():
        try:
            data, addr = sock.recvfrom(512)
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
        except OSError:
            break
        if data.strip() == P.DISCOVERY_MAGIC:
            reply = P.DISCOVERY_REPLY + (":%d" % tcp_port).encode("ascii")
            try:
                sock.sendto(reply, addr)
                if verbose:
                    sys.stderr.write("[master] probe from %s\n" % (addr[0],))
            except OSError:
                pass
    sock.close()



def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Call of Acaristan KRAPNET master")
    ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1",
                    help="bind address (use 0.0.0.0 to serve a LAN)")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=P.DEFAULT_MASTER_PORT)
    ap.add_argument("--discovery-port", type=int, default=P.DISCOVERY_PORT)
    ap.add_argument("--no-discovery", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--no-seed", action="store_true",
                    help="start with zero servers instead of the fictional set")
    ap.add_argument("-q", "--quiet", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    verbose = not args.quiet
    state = MasterState(seed=not args.no_seed)
    try:
        server = ThreadedTCPServer((args.host, args.port), MasterHandler,
                                   state, verbose)
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[master] cannot bind %s:%d -- %s\n" % (
            args.host, args.port, exc))
        return 1

    stop_evt = threading.Event()
    if not args.no_discovery:
        threading.Thread(target=run_discovery,
                         args=(args.discovery_port, args.port, stop_evt, verbose),
                         daemon=True).start()

    def _sig(_signum, _frame):
        stop_evt.set()
        server.stopping = True
        # shutdown() blocks until serve_forever returns, so it must not be
        # called from the signal handler's own thread.
        threading.Thread(target=server.shutdown, daemon=True).start()

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _sig)
    try:
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _sig)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, OSError):
        pass  # SIGTERM does not exist on Windows

    sys.stderr.write("[master] listening on %s:%d  (proto %d)\n" % (
        args.host, args.port, P.PROTO_VERSION))
    sys.stderr.write("[master] seeded %d servers%s\n" % (
        len(state.servers),
        "" if args.no_seed else "  (--no-seed to start empty)"))
    sys.stderr.flush()
    try:
        server.serve_forever(poll_interval=0.2)
    finally:
        stop_evt.set()
        server.server_close()
        sys.stderr.write("[master] stopped\n")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
